sites.name: The Parliament
sites.note: The Republic's political core, a grand white marble edifice symbolising peace and hope; it hosts public debates and confidential chambers.

sites.name: Arena of Future
sites.note: Popular arena of safe, magical, non-lethal bouts and monthly tournaments; an inactive Vandanamalika lies beneath it.

sites.name: Republic Military Fortress
sites.note: Built atop a natural plateau, it houses magical cannons and the headquarters of the Freelands' military forces.

sites.name: Prime Minister's Palace
sites.note: Home of the head of government and administrative heart of many ministries; hosts a monthly gala.

sites.name: Celestianist Cathedral of Sun and Moon
sites.note: The Republic's primary Celestianist temple under High Cardinal Taram, now the administrative heart of the Church.

sites.name: Fisherman's Wharf Port
sites.note: The Republic's largest and most militarized port; abundant fish and seafood, most trade ships sail to Kolbjörn.

sites.name: Seabreeze District
sites.note: Serene middle-class enclave of merchants, artisans, fishing ship owners, military officers and bureaucrats.

sites.name: The Six Quarters
sites.note: Surrounding the Parliament, the city's priciest estates; its sole non-residential structure is the Relic Hunters Guild headquarters.

sites.name: Wallside District
sites.note: Inhabited by winter elves and eyed with mistrust; Kemet spies hide among them around a concealed temple to Bás.

sites.name: Uptown
sites.note: Hilly district of diverse shops and estates, with the open market and the Adventurer's Guild headquarters atop a hill.

sites.name: Hope Square
sites.note: Home to laborers and farming families resettled after the Kemet Invasion; the Academy of Magic stands on its edge; crime is rife.

sites.name: The Cerulean Plaza
sites.note: The commercial heart, a bustling market of white and blue facades with inns, taverns and the Cerulean Cross Hotel.

world.name: Tanares
world.description: Le monde et ses lieux. Geographie de reference : carte du monde VTT.

central-empire.name: Central Empire
central-empire.description: The center of power of the Tanarean Empire, the most powerful Empire under absolute control of Emperor Baleroth, the Faceless Emperor.

imperial-benenet.name: Imperial Benênet
imperial-benenet.description: Province dominated by the Tanarean Empire, ruled by a governor appointed by Emperor Baleroth.

kingdom-of-kolbjorn.name: Kingdom of Kolbjörn
kingdom-of-kolbjorn.description: The entire territory is ruled by a king, who delegates to his Jarls the responsibility of governing each region, all under the banner of the Tanarean Empire.

magocracy-of-mage-tower.name: Magocracy of Mage Tower
magocracy-of-mage-tower.description: Magocratic regime headed by a council containing one representative from each specialty.

republic-of-freelands.name: Republic of Freelands
republic-of-freelands.description: The Republic of Freelands holds a democratic system with a parliament led by a Prime Minister.

seashores.name: Seashores
seashores.description: Officially it is still an Imperial province, but it is governed by the Pirate Lords of the Parliament of the Seas, in agreement with Emperor Baleroth.

sindile-forest.name: Sindile Forest
sindile-forest.description: Governed by a high council of Spring elves, whose last word is a couple, a King and a Queen, who hold office temporarily.

storm-islands.name: Storm Islands
storm-islands.description: Ruled by Gullog, the Deathbringer, in league with Bás, the elven deity of winter and death.

stravian-domains.name: Stravian Domains
stravian-domains.description: Governed by the three Dwarf Kings of the underground Kingdom of Stonelair, keeping all surface communities under their rule.

taii-maku-city-states.name: Taii’Maku City States
taii-maku-city-states.description: With no unified government, each Illu is its independent city-state ruled by a council of the greatest minds. Each year, the Illus sends representatives to a gathering of knowledge exchange to discuss shared goals.

theocracy-of-kepesh.name: Theocracy of Kepesh
theocracy-of-kepesh.description: Governed by the religion dedicated to Ba-ka, whose main representative is the Pharaoh Lich Kalistessenâmun.

tsvetan.name: Tsvetan
tsvetan.description: Fragmented into two groups of clans, each claiming to have their legitimate War Lord and Red Mother.

yama.name: Yama
yama.description: Ruled by the eldest tameranium dragon, Fumetsu Tenshikin, the Emperor sanctified as a deity dwelling amidst his devoted adherents, beneath whom stand the clergy and the clans forged by the most distinguished lineages.

central-empire-ancient-heargs.name: Ancient Heargs
central-empire-ancient-heargs.description: Deep in the heart of the Bak Forest western region lies an ancient stone circle, the Ancient Heargs, revered as the druids’ holiest site. This sacred enclave is the nexus of ancient magic that defends the forest. The site is a breathtaking clearing with twelve stone effigies engraved with druidic symbols, lush grass, and radiant flowers, channeling the forest’s energy. Outsiders are not allowed near the Heargs, save for a few who gained the trust of its guardians. The spirits that appear here are not mere apparitions but the will of nature’s diverse facets. Some personify nature’s benevolence, while others reflect its brutality, but all seek to defend Tanares against the Ungods. Rumors say that the magic in the Heargs has roots in the Godly Age, when magic and knowledge, now lost to mortals, flourished. This ancient origin has drawn the interest of many organizations eager to unearth its secrets. Close to the Heargs resides the lair of a couple of ancient green dragons that protect an isolated Draconic Tower in Bak Forest. These dragons are not merely allies of the druids; they are among the earliest to tap into nature’s magic in Tanares, having waged war against the Ungods since their invasion. They imparted the ways to many mortals, and to this day, they partake in rituals and the defense of the forest, yet a shadow has recently befallen them; their youngest progeny has vanished. The dragons, deeply troubled by this loss, believe it has been taken away to the Penumbral Plane by cultists of Z’ulvath. The druids seek adventurers to go into the Penumbral Plane for a rescue mission, fearing the young dragon may be used against its kin.

These fungi, releasing hallucinogenic spores, are rumored to grant visions of potential futures. Amidst the eucalyptus trees and vibrant green moss, there are no animals, as here dwells fungal entities and plant beings such as myconids, violent fungus, otyughs, and treants, with many treants bearing fungal growths adorning their trunks and leaves. The fungus demonstrates collective intelligence, enabling it to sense and communicate across the forest. Though its purpose is mysterious, whispers suggest it may be a cursed human transformed into this state. The infected treants are under the fungus’ control, while myconids and other fungal creatures remain free, with the myconids even venerating the fungus as a deity despite receiving no divine magic in return. central-empire-hajal-city.name: Hajal City
central-empire-hajal-city.description: A global financial center, it hosts the Bank of Hajal’s main office. The city’s cold climate and seasonal gardens complement its elegant, multicultural design, reflecting its Soulborn founders’ culture. Residents adhere to strict social hierarchies and etiquette, and even the least affluent earn above-average wages, but attire varies by class. The wealthy don formal outfits and fine jewelry, traveling in lavish carriages. The middle class wears long coats and leather boots for style and warmth. Lower-class citizens use work-specific attire, usually marked by employer-specific pins or buttons. Employment is a badge of honor, symbolized by well-kept clothing, while the jobless wear rugged outfits. Though Imperial Law and the Ironhands are present, the Bank essentially rules Hajal because of an old deal with Emperor Baleroth. Attracting visitors from across Tanares, Hajal is a hub for those seeking wealth or investment. However, predatory contracts, idea theft, and even blackmail are rampant here. Rumors of debt-induced servitude hint at the city’s darker aspects. The many wealthy individuals in the city make it ripe for adventurers looking for powerful patrons. Bank investors are always looking for competent individuals to protect their investments in distant lands or to enforce contracts on those unwilling to keep their part. Recently, the Third Eye has been infiltrating the city, slowly building up power to place agents in the higher positions of the Bank. While the Council of Investors of the Bank has received notice of strange movements in the city, they are imprecise. The Councilors are offering high payments to lure great investigators, adventurers, and spies to uncover what is happening in their city.
central-empire-hajal-city.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

central-empire-odraz-monastery.name: Odraz Monastery
central-empire-odraz-monastery.description: Located at the southern foot of the Rainbow Dale mountains, on the extreme western edge of the Central Empire, Tamera’s devotees have maintained the Odraz monastery for centuries. Its alabaster walls are adorned with carvings of angels, saints, monks, and paladins. Those who attain the status of saints and heroes of the church may have statues carved here honoring them. Hundreds of monks and priests keep the monastery’s daily routine of prayer, study, and meditation, but what makes Odraz famous is its unique martial art—created centuries ago by Odraz’s traveling preachers who returned from distant lands, bringing back insights about Yama’s unique blend of meditation and physical training for self-improvement and fusing it with the Odraz paladins’ training. By combining physical exercises, combat training, weapon drills, meditation, and prayer, they have developed a unique style that blends faith, inner strength, weapon mastery, and hand-to-hand combat. Odraz primarily admits young recruits chosen through the meditative divination of Odraz masters. Other individuals wishing to learn from them must offer substantial donations and agree to perform services for Odraz, usually helping small communities and facing evil creatures as a test of their worth. Individuals may be accepted for training at Odraz if they approach the tasks with sincerity, dedication, and a genuine desire to assist those in need. Rumors suggest that the monastery houses a sacred torch, crafted by a saint and blessed by Tamera. This artifact would be the only one capable of completely illuminating areas within the Penumbral Plane. While the true origin or power of the artifact remains a mystery, the monks do their utmost to protect their secret vault from intruders.
central-empire-odraz-monastery.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

central-empire-phantom-fortress.name: Phantom Fortress
central-empire-phantom-fortress.description: Located just miles from the Capital, the stronghold doubles as an Ironhand fortress and maximum-security prison. Its fifty-foot walls, patrolled by guards, house high-risk prisoners and reinforce the Capital’s defenses. The stronghold sports a cruciform layout surrounded by a circular wall, dividing it into four courtyards, with a wide tower at its center. The Ironhand army occupies three wings and the tower’s upper levels, while the prison takes one wing and the tower’s lower and underground floors. Once an ancient wizard’s lab, the tower’s underground now serves as an “open jail.” Prisoners roam chambers circling a dark abyss, seemingly free, yet trapped. Amenities like a sunlit garden, an Imperial propaganda-filled library, and a temple to Tamera and Bauron serve to indoctrinate them. But the ghosts haunting their sleep are the prison’s worst feature, slowly eroding mental resistance to turn prisoners into complacency. Named after these ghosts, rumored to have been slain wizards in Baleroth’s quest for mystical knowledge, the stronghold also houses special isolation cells warded by antimagic fields to deal with dangerous prisoners. Magic wards and alarms secure the entire facility. On the military front, hundreds of soldiers stand ready to quell any military threat or escape attempts. A ritual chamber exists at the top of the tower, used for converting individuals into Ironhand soldiers by psychosurgery using tameranium and bauronite to strip them of free will. Many criminals, rebels, and captured spies are sent to this fortress, which also makes it a target for prison break attempts. The allied forces have a deep interest in releasing a few of the prisoners that are here. At the same time, the Empire uses this place to extract information or keep individuals who can be held for ransom, possessing value for other political forces. Some scholars believe that the ghosts here are bound by powerful magic from Baleroth himself, and they hold unique knowledge about the psychosurgery that creates Ironhands. Rumors say freeing these souls could allow one to gain their vast arcane knowledge or mystical powers.
central-empire-phantom-fortress.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

central-empire-skybell-city.name: Skybell City
central-empire-skybell-city.description: This blessed city hosts the holiest Celestianist Cathedral, a pilgrimage site steeped in legend. It’s said that angels gathered here to fight the Ungods ages ago. The Cathedral conceals ancient artifacts, scriptures, and the tombs of holy figures. Rumors suggest it even holds angelic relics. Though under Imperial jurisdiction, the Cathedral grounds follow Celestianist law and are protected by its paladins, a legacy of an ancient pact with Emperor Baleroth. The city’s central market thrives due to pilgrims across Tanares offering many goods. However, non-Celestianist followers are not welcome; no other temples exist, and while the practice of other religions is not illegal, it is clear that such worship is seen as an affront to the local populace. The Cult of Shadow Wing aims to corrupt Skybell. They almost succeeded before the Celestianist Reform and now regroup in hidden corners. Their agenda includes corrupting clergy, undermining people’s faith, and fostering counter-reform to revert the Church to its original Evolutionist dogma. By creating false hints of corruption against the Church leaders, they seek to manipulate public opinion. Though the Church has countered its efforts, Skybell remains the focal point of the Cult’s activities.
central-empire-skybell-city.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

central-empire-the-great-forest-of-bak.name: The Great Forest of Bak
central-empire-the-great-forest-of-bak.description: Divided into Western and Eastern regions, it is the continent’s second-largest forest, safeguarded by an Imperial Decree. This protection was secured by Thalia in the Arena of Fate, defending the druids’ rights, which Baleroth used to showcase his supposed desire to enforce the Arena’s judgments, even against the Empire. Bak is no ordinary forest; it boasts healing ponds that cause plants to grow into exceptional beauty while ancient spells guard its core. This verdant sanctuary is home to the most extraordinary druidic circle of Tanares, devout followers of the Nature Spirits. Their deep connection with Bak offers them unique gifts: resurrection powers
central-empire-the-great-forest-of-bak.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

imperial-benenet-begraense.name: Begraense
imperial-benenet-begraense.description: The fortified capital of Ben’net stands at the foot of towering glaciers, its icy walls protecting its northern flank, while the Frostflow River’s cold, turbulent waters cover its eastern side. The city rises on several concentric plateaus, each encircled by walls that limit access to unauthorized persons. Here, the Ironhand’s vigilance is strict, yielding an impeccable organization and negligible crime. The densest population resides in the lower tiers, marked by inns and stables. Ascending zones, one can find merchant shops, temples, and garrisons, culminating in the central Nobles’ Ward, where one can find Governor Bonas Weyrdo’s palace. Beneath the city lie concealed passages and subterranean chambers, facilitating the swift deployment of Ironhand troops and housing prisons and hidden halls. This network allows soldiers to appear abruptly when trouble arises, with entry points scattered throughout the city. Begraense allows cirrus and envoys from other factions, like the Allied Forces and the Arcanum, to enter but keeps them under close surveillance. Despite the stringent regulations of the city, an underground black market thrives, trading in Highlandtuber Distillate, magic items, and other prohibited goods. It is controlled by a figure known as “The Veiled Baron,” who allegedly has ties to the Imperial echelons and the Bloodbound Mafia. This hub offers rare goods and information, and its existence under Governor Bonas’ jurisdiction is rumored to have resulted from a deal with the Baron. Adventurers and mercenaries can often find work here, from commoners seeking aid they cannot find with the Ironhand, such as to find disappeared family members, to members of the Third Eye seeking individuals to perform dangerous tasks, to hidden rebels trying to incite the populace against the Empire by seeking help to expose the misdeeds of Governor Bonnas. Many more factions are seeking capable hands than those willing to venture into this harsh, cold north, so plenty of tasks are available.
imperial-benenet-begraense.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

imperial-benenet-crystal-mountains.name: Crystal Mountains
imperial-benenet-crystal-mountains.description: The cirrus communities perch high up on the Crystal Mountains, breathtaking in their austere beauty. Their architecture, a marvel of design with towering structures, balances gracefully on the mountain peaks, embodying the freedom the cirrus cherish. Access to these cities is a feat, typically requiring magical or aerial means due to the treacherous mountain terrain. Since not all cirrus possess wings to fly, many of them rely on winged creatures as mounts, which can be seen constantly patrolling the skies. The seven largest communities are governed each by one of the seven Zephyr Knights Orders. Historically, the Evolutionist Church and the Tanarean Empire have sought to catalog these settlements, but the persistent mists cloak their boundaries, obscuring where one community ends and another begins. For centuries, alchemists and wizards have attempted to explore these mountains to collect unique herbs unavailable anywhere else in Tanares. However, the harsh terrain and the cirrus’ distrust often make it challenging to obtain these rare components. This often leads adventurers and mercenaries to climb the mountains for flowers or leaves that can earn them significant rewards. Due to their inaccessibility and strong defenses, the Tanarean Empire has never threatened these communities. Still, the same cannot be said of Thundraxa. This penumbral dragon has established its lair in the vicinity of Dark Glacier and has been corrupting white dragons in the region to unleash their fury against the communities of the Crystal Mountains. The elder cirrus defends the hypothesis that these attacks are merely a ruse to camouflage an ongoing plan that the creature is executing.
imperial-benenet-crystal-mountains.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

imperial-benenet-mistvale.name: Mistvale
imperial-benenet-mistvale.description: The region of Mistvale is shrouded in dense mists and frost that have long characterized its name. Of late, these conditions have worsened; the fog’s chill intensifies to lethal levels within its radius, claiming the lives of the unwary. These victims rise as frozen undead, preying upon travelers from Ben’net’s eastern reaches and fueling speculation about the source of this curse. The Tanarean Empire, preoccupied with the cirrus communities and wary of aiding Baleroth’s schemes, neglects Mistvale. Only with the use of magic can one safely navigate its frigid haze. In truth, the Darkall Forces, led by Gullog and the priests of Bás, are the culprits. They’ve erected a sanctuary for Bás, the Goddess of Winter and Death. Their goals are twofold: to extend Bás’ dominion, forge an undead legion, and access the cirrus cities in the mountains where their many ancient artifacts and magic knowledge are stored, which could greatly benefit the Kemets. They are sending incursions of undead to the nearby Plateaus of Eternal Ice, where cirrus warriors and the Arcanum congregate for training, who are now facing the peril of the undead emerging from Mistvale.
imperial-benenet-mistvale.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

kingdom-of-kolbjorn-falun-mountain.name: Falun Mountain
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-falun-mountain.description: Falun, the Valkyries’ sacred city, floats atop the towering peaks of the Maëd Range as a sanctuary closed off to outsiders, and those few invited in find a wondrous sight. The stone structures are carved with sacred symbols in gold while the streets are taken by valkyries sharpening their weapons, writing and singing epic poems, or riding their pegasus in patrols. At the center is the temple dedicated to the spirits, encircled by many communal halls. Here, the valkyries prepare themselves for the ultimate battle against the Ungods while searching for valorous heroes for them to guide. The Valkyries believe that their holy power comes from the poems and legends kept stored in the temple vaults, which hold the essence of the praised heroes. A claim they prove with unaging bodies and holy powers. Their creed stands that on the day of the final battle against the Ungods, the spirit of these legendary individuals will infuse their bodies and allow them to show their true strength. During battles, it is common to see Valkyries soaring in the skies, protecting heroes, or searching for new champions. They often nurture those with great potential, but only those they deem honorable. Those who betray them or lose their honor while being guided are hunted down for being potential servants of the Ungods. While the Valkyries travel the continent searching for individuals to guide, they rarely involve themselves in mortal affairs, preferring to drive people to solve their own problems. However, their honorable and benevolent nature may cause one to intercede, especially if extraplanar forces are involved. Currently, the Valkyries are seeking champions to stop the spread of Bás Temples in the west islands and to venture into the Mystical region to recover lost artifacts in the ruins.
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-falun-mountain.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

kingdom-of-kolbjorn-great-valley.name: Great Valley
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-great-valley.description: In the shadow of the towering Godspire Mountains lies the ancient lands of the giants. This majestic valley, partitioned among the giant kin, has thrived by upholding ancient pacts of peace with the humans to the south and between the giant kinds themselves. The Pact gave rise to the One Council, an assembly where leaders of each giant kind meet to deliberate the affairs of the valley and ensure the sacred vows of their ancestors endured. At each solstice, or when an emergency meeting is required, the One Council is held in the Earth and Sky Temple, a magnificent colossal tower of stone and crystal at the center of the valley protected by powerful magical wards. Yet, the once harmonious coexistence has frayed at the edges, simmering toward conflict. A titan named Abhorroth, consumed by the corruption of the Ungods, has cast a shadow over the region. He has sown discord, swaying the younger and the power-hungry among the giants and casting aspersions to suggest the humans, the Kolbjörners, have forsaken the old Pact. Though the most sensible of the elder giants remain impervious to his machinations, those who have allied with him have formed what is now known as the Giant Empire. This burgeoning coalition, open to all giantkind, seeks to usurp the valley and ignite a war against Kolbjörn. In their eyes, the battle is for the birth of a Giant Empire; for Abhorroth, it is a means to an end—a massacre intended to invoke a Malrokian Curse to empower his master, Droggath.
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-great-valley.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

kingdom-of-kolbjorn-irongauntlet.name: Irongauntlet
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-irongauntlet.description: Irongauntlet, an ancient dwarven citadel, sits atop the Maëd Range. Abandoned by the dwarves ages ago, it is now a fortified human city. The citadel’s design made it an invulnerable refuge for Kolbjörn’s people, with a bustling village at its gate. The economy is based on miners and blacksmiths, depending on its trade to survive. The city also serves as a shelter, as during winter or wars, people from many villages in Kolbjörn are guided to hide in Irongauntlet underground citadel. People live in a village on the surface, as the dwarven citadel is a maze of tunnels and hidden paths where miners venture to gather ore. Yet, recently, the roar of unknown creatures has been echoing there, and small earthquakes are causing destruction and fatalities. Some shamans interpret these as mountain spirits’ anger, believing a misdeed of one or a group of miners. The inhabitants are divided. The Stonecircle group attributes the tremors to lurking monsters. They advocate for sealing off the mines and reinforcing structures to prevent collapses. On the other hand, the Mountain Warriors argue that the solution lies in facing these creatures head-on. They fear that closing the passages will lead the monsters to increase, amplifying the earthquakes and destroying the city. Meanwhile, the Spirit Whispers see the tremors as messages from the spirits. They claim that closing or venturing into the mountains will worsen the situation and believe in doing sacred rituals, sacrifices, and finding who angered the spirits to punish them. As iron reserves dwindle, miners and blacksmiths face a looming famine. They are torn between the shamans and warriors while dreading the Stonecircle solution. Amidst the turmoil, groups recruit adventurers for support, with the Mountain Warriors seeking heroes to venture into the undergrounds. While the truth is unknown, the Kolbjörners may soon know why the dwarves abandoned Irongauntlet.
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-irongauntlet.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

kingdom-of-kolbjorn-kolbjorn-capital.name: Kolbjörn Capital
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-kolbjorn-capital.description: Nestled in a river valley and serving as the capital, the city is known for its stone bridges that connect neighborhoods around the Ygfall Fortress, the King’s home. It is renowned for boasting the major clans’ common houses, the large shipyards, the forges of famous blacksmiths, and the halls of expert leatherworkers. However, only those with a father and a grandfather born in Kolbjörn can live inside the walls; others must live in the external district or a unique separated stone walled section built for the servants of the Empire. Because of torrential rains and floods, the city constructions are elevated, with tunnels and chambers below to drain water. Unfortunately, these often attract criminals who want to move around undetected. However, during rain, the tunnels can suddenly fill with water, resulting in yearly drowings. Recently, a secret cult began to gather criminals and the discontented in the tunnels. Led by “The Rat Jarl,” a rat lycanthrope passing himself as a blessed one from a lost lineage, they are building a secret lair. Using magic and cunning masonry, he protects these lairs from flooding, creating a criminal haven while turning the most loyal servants into wererats to “spread his blessing.” The Rat Jarl is a Third Eye member in ascension, using this ploy to gather information and gain wealth. Unknown to his lackeys, he lives covertly in the Imperial District as an Imperial Tax collector. The King and the Empire are aware of the rise of crime and bandits fleeing to the sewers. However, they have already lost good men who drowned while investigating. The King has placed a bounty on these criminals and especially on their unknown leader.
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-kolbjorn-capital.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

kingdom-of-kolbjorn-northharbor.name: Northharbor
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-northharbor.description: This bustling port city thrives on trade with the Freelands and Kepesh Theocracy. Ruled by a savvy Jarl from the Walrus Clan, known as a tough seafarer, the city’s harbors are its soul, full of colorful masts of Drakkars and the resonant noise of commerce. The people of Northarbor, hardened by the freezing waters in which they swim from youth, are renowned as the most enduring warriors. Though they are the most pacifist and diplomatic clans, they possess great tenacity and can become terrifyingly violent when provoked, traits they believe mirror the walrus displayed on their flags. Yet beneath the surface of this vibrant trade center, tensions arise between the revolutionaries and the imperial loyalists as whispers of treason and dishonor spread. While alliances forged in commerce with the Republic have strengthened some bonds, others believe staying with the Empire is necessary to avoid war. Amidst these internal struggles, they must stand against the sea threat as the Kemets’ fleet has seized significant portions of the Dead Island Archipelago, bringing a creeping mystical winter from their temples of Bás, along with their hordes of undead. The Walrus Clan and the city of Northarbor stand defiant, safeguarding their home and fighting to stop the Kemets from advancing into the continent.
kingdom-of-kolbjorn-northharbor.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

magocracy-of-mage-tower-arcane-universit.name: Arcane University
magocracy-of-mage-tower-arcane-universit.description: Next to the Dawn of Light city, there is an immense campus of the largest arcane university in Tanares. With eight large towers, one for each school of magic, and many other structures, including a small floating island, it is the best place to learn spells. It is full of large halls with decorations based on arcane spells and corridors connecting various locations. Legends even speak of a vast dungeon underground. Families pay large amounts of gold for their children’s admission; still, there is a long waiting list. It is both a place of study and competition; from early on, students are motivated to elevate the prestige of their respective towers above the others. The time required to earn an arcane certificate is ten years, with four years of basic subjects, four years for advanced subjects, and another two years for specialization. Many tests occur along the way, and only a third of the initial students complete the course. This place is mainly enhanced by magic and contains many interesting features: Arcane Mirrors. Students have in their rooms a special mirror capable of communicating with other students and their tutors. Living paintings. Some paintings move, showing a sequence of actions for learning or entertainment purposes. Chrono Chamber. Inside this room, the time passes ten times slower than the outside. It is used when students need to study before the tests. On the floating islands, there are some locations related to each school tower: • Abjuration: The Barrier Wards • Conjuration: The Summoning Circle • Divination: The Oracle’s Pool • Enchantment: Hall of Whispers • Evocation: The Arcane Arenas • Illusion: The Mirage Labyrinth • Necromancy: The Ancestral Tombs • Transmutation: The Alchemical Gardens
magocracy-of-mage-tower-arcane-universit.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

magocracy-of-mage-tower-asylum-eberek.name: Asylum Eberek
magocracy-of-mage-tower-asylum-eberek.description: In a remote place of Alkira Mountain, there is a powerful magical construction that receives visits from people across all Tanares. It is made of marble and gems, many of which have a pulsating shine. This asylum has a unique feature. When an individual is admitted to this place, others gradually forget about this person, taking up to an entire month for them to be fully forgotten. This means that anyone might have a family member there whom they have forgotten about. It is a very convenient place, as people can abandon members of their families without carrying the guilt of this action. In around one month, the creature starts to live in an illusion of life through a dream, varying in the time they experience. Freeing someone at this stage is almost impossible. Recently, the wizard Alina from the Council developed a powerful spell allowing a group to project into the Astral Plane, enter the individual’s dreams, and retrieve their consciousness by convincing them to wake up from the dream’s illusion. Some reports suggest these dreams can be extremely dangerous, as fears and hidden secrets may manifest to the group in various forms. If a person dies in the dream, their soul must be recovered first from there before any resurrection attempt can be made.
magocracy-of-mage-tower-asylum-eberek.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

magocracy-of-mage-tower-crystal-tower.name: Crystal Tower
magocracy-of-mage-tower-crystal-tower.description: The Crystal Tower, one of the most mysterious places in Tanares, has stood tall since the Ancient Age. It is a massive tower with one hundred floors and a large tameranium crystal on its top. Constructed by the Kemets, the tower is a remarkable blend of engineering and magic, possessing unique characteristics that have never been replicated. It is a place for extensive research and study, where the Arcane Council members work, and they govern from the Mage Tower. Before Avelum departed for the Republic, he warned that some secrets within the tower were too dangerous to be utilized. He cast powerful spells to seal parts of the tower and its underground chambers. Many wizards are now working to dispel these protections and access its mysteries. The tower possesses many defense mechanisms and traps, and records indicate that its underground contains a dungeon full of extraplanar creatures summoned by the ancient wizards to protect the place.
magocracy-of-mage-tower-crystal-tower.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

magocracy-of-mage-tower-magic-duel-arena.name: Magic Duel Arena
magocracy-of-mage-tower-magic-duel-arena.description: This arena was built for wizards to demonstrate their might in a safe environment. It is a vast, oval-shaped arena protected with a dozen magic barriers. Initially, it was used for wizards to duel but was later adapted to host group fights for sport and training. After some time, new styles of combat appeared, such as: • A group must defeat a magic simulacrum of one or more creatures, simulating powerful monsters. • A group gains 7 wands of wizard spells (three from 1st level, two from 2nd level, and one from 3rd and 4th levels). Each has four charges and is given before the combat starts. Non-wizards can use these wands, but they must use two charges for each use of the spell. No attacks or spells except those from these wands can be used during these trials.
magocracy-of-mage-tower-magic-duel-arena.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

magocracy-of-mage-tower-mesoriver.name: Mesoriver
magocracy-of-mage-tower-mesoriver.description: The region’s most developed and notable city has earned the title of capital for being the magical city of Tanares. The city is composed of many towers, floating islands, and even castles levitating, with many trying to display their wealth and power. With many tameranium pylons and elemental creatures spread throughout the city, many magic items are powered by the auras of minerals. It is possible to find many curious features: • Houses with living architecture capable of shape changing; • Transportation options include disks, flying boats, transportation circles, and flying carriages for romantic purposes; • Magical utilities: while within the city, many devices and wands can create day-to-day effects, like everburn fire to illuminate places; • Extensive use of illusions for entertainment purposes, like showing magical beasts, dragons combats, and many others; • Perfect weather control to create pleasant temperatures or, in some specific areas, be either cold or hot. However, despite its magnificence, this city harbors many dangers. Some spells may cause explosions, elementals can get loose and attack people, summonings can go out of control, and the teleportation circle may malfunction and send people to unsafe areas. Recently, two major concerns have frightened people in the city. A powerful mastermind invoked from the Elemental Plane is trying to release the elementals, and some wizards have been disappearing from the higher towers without a trace. The Arcane Enforcers are investigating but recruiting adventurers to assist them.
magocracy-of-mage-tower-mesoriver.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

magocracy-of-mage-tower-summer-island.name: Summer Island
magocracy-of-mage-tower-summer-island.description: The mysterious and magnificent tropical island, nestled amidst the frozen mountains of Reginheraht, remains an enigma yet to be understood. Created by Kelorth, the White Avatar Dragon, this island serves as both a resting place and a unique training ground for dragonblades. Its elemental magic-infused landscape climate greatly contrasts the surrounding region. The island’s warm climate, inviting beaches, and friendly fauna attract visitors from across Tanares, especially nobles, drawn to its hot waters. At the heart of the island, near the volcano’s base, lies a portal to an extraplanar dungeon called “The Elemental Grounds.” With its deserts, lava wastelands, and towering freezing mountains, this mysterious realm is home to gargantuan animals, aggressive elementals, and aberrant hybrid creatures. However, explorers must be cautious, as the portal’s arrival location within this treacherous land shifts unpredictably each day. The shining tower, built at its center as a beacon for dragonblades, offers the only hope of return. Despite the danger, the portal lures many curious and brave. It leads to numerous rescue missions for those lost within its depths, despite the constant vigilance at its entrance to avoid such accidents. Curiously, creatures from this extraplanar dungeon cannot pass through the portal into Tanares; they dissolve upon attempting it. Dragonblades frequently venture into this portal searching for combat experience, often in groups. Kelorth intended this place to be a test and training for his army, preparing them for battle against the Ungods. It’s a rite of passage for Kelorth’s servants and even young dragons from his tower to brave this place at least once. The ultimate reward for reaching the central shining tower is an audience with Kelorth himself, a coveted opportunity for adventurers seeking the counsel of this powerful being or to plead their case directly to the Draconic Council leaders. Plane’s Elemental Nature. Each location in the Elemental Grounds is saturated with an element—Fire, Water, Earth, or Air. Creatures spawned in each area deal an additional 1d6 damage of that elemental type (fire, cold, acid for earth, or lighting for air) with their attacks and are immune to damage from it.
magocracy-of-mage-tower-summer-island.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-aurindunnum.name: Aurindunnum
republic-of-freelands-aurindunnum.description: Soaring in the skies, the capital city of the autumn elves floats above the Republic’s northern expanse. A blend of city and fortress, its autumnal glow, waterfalls, and spires are shaped by both tangible materials and unique illusion magic turned solid by intricate rituals. This magic allows the city to float amidst clouds, showcasing unique structures like levitating staircases and the orbiting spheres of light that brighten its nights, as well as granting all its residents illusory wings that allow flight. To shield Aurindunnum, robust abjuration wards stand, and countless air elementals are bound for its defense. Once in ruins, King Sundaryll regained hope when he fell in love with Anariel during the Kemet Invasion. Seeing the Republic as a chance for rebirth, and with the assistance of Archmage Avelum and High Cardinal Taram, the city was revitalized. However, challenges persist. The Cult of Shadow Wing often makes it a target of their assaults, and the Empire sees the airborne fortress as a threat, especially because of its alignment with the Republic. Yet, the gravest threat is internal, as Prince Quizzarian, Sundaryll’s younger brother, both brilliant and mad, is always working on plans to take the throne from his brother. Quizzarian plans go from harmless pranks to dangerous gambits to undermine Sundaryll. Whether it’s entrapping the King in a maze, magically enhancing monsters, breaking Sundaryll’s scepter and hiding the parts, or unleashing a plague with one unique cure, Quizzarian’s actions are always wrapped in riddles and intricate traps. His goal? To prove his intellectual superiority. Further complicating matters, Sundaryll must lead monthly ventures into the Penumbral Plane to gather energy from aberrations and emoguns. This energy sustains Aurindunnum’s defenses and keeps it airborne. Joined by Anariel and the mystical knights, riding Stormbirds of the god Aibidh, they are often seeking mercenaries and adventurers to help with specific threats or tasks during these missions.
republic-of-freelands-aurindunnum.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-city-of-heroes-ris.name: City of Heroes Rise
republic-of-freelands-city-of-heroes-ris.description: Situated in a valley surrounded by hills, Heroes Rise was established by the Resistance during the Kemet Invasion and originally named Wharfugee. Its strategic location, combined with ancient druidic magic, made it an ideal site for constructing a hidden village. Over weeks of work, the Resistance fortified the city, creating what now is a symbol of the courage and resilience that gave birth to the Republic. Now, Heroes Rise stands as the cherished historical jewel of the Republic, capturing the spark that defied both the Kemets and the Empire. The city draws young adventurers, housing a major branch of the Adventurer’s Guild. Many believe starting their adventurer’s career here brings good fortune, luring countless aspiring heroes. Notable residents include Avelum, Tanares’ mightiest archmage; Zalir, the Relic Hunters’ founder; Sara, the seer who owns Tanares most prestigious tavern; and Sir Erick, the noble paladin and current Lord Mayor of Heroes Rise. Together with other legends of the Kemet Invasion, they turn Heroes Rise into the city of living legends. Heroes Rise’s streets pulse with optimism. Crime and poverty are rare, and the community’s bond, forged during wartime, remains strong. However, the Cult of Shadow Wing seeks to destroy the city, recognizing its significance in the hearts and minds of people across Tanares. The Cult wants to make the city an example of what happens to the enemies of their dark lords. High Cardinal Taram and the Celestianist Church also consider the city crucial due to a secret prophecy about a child or group of children destined to shape the world of Tanares. Uncertain if the Ungods’ followers are aware of the prophecy, they keep it closely guarded. Both Razun and Taram stay vigilant to safeguard all children of the city, ensuring that the city orphanage provides exceptional care to every child.
republic-of-freelands-city-of-heroes-ris.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf.name: Fisherman’s Wharf
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf.description: Population: Approximately 570,000. Leadership: Governed by the current elected Lord Mayor Jessa. It hosts the Parliament, and the Republic Ministers, including Prime Minister Tellatius Military Strength: The Republic has around 4,100 soldiers in the city. From a once-humble fishing village, Fisherman’s Wharf rose to a bustling metropolis with the Empire’s investments before it became part of the Republic. Emperor Baleroth intended to create a Vandanamalika here, hidden underneath the Arena of Future’s construction, aiming to use the unique positioning of the city to activate it during the Lunar Perigee. However, the Kemet Invasion disrupted these plans. The city’s architecture, with towering stone edifices amid simpler wooden buildings, showcases its rapid growth under the Empire. Now, the red banners of the Empire were exchanged for the calming blues of the Republic, while statues and symbols of the Empire were replaced with monuments honoring the heroes of the Kemet Invasion. Fisherman’s Wharf, hosting the Republic’s parliament and the Freelands’ busiest port, hums with ceaseless activity. Yet, Kemet invaders from the Storm Islands frequently challenge its prosperity. Though the city lacks formalized noble districts, its center draws the wealthy for its proximity to the parliament, raising real estate prices. The middle class favors the coast, while the less affluent find a home near the city walls, where property remains affordable, except near the gates, where shops, inns, and taverns fight over space. In the Main Hall of the Adventurer’s Guild, one can find many quests and employment opportunities, while in the Relic Hunters Headquarters, explorers can expect generous rewards for bringing ancient relics and texts. But beneath this tranquil exterior, political games play out. The city teems with high-society events and covert meetings, all centered around power plays. Currently, a faction of nobles is working to incite civil unrest and inflate crime rates, all to destabilize society, aiming to increase their influence in the upcoming elections. Believing the Republic lacks a robust authority figure, they seek to secure many parliamentary seats under the pretense of creating more strict laws against crime and then appoint a new prime minister, all to gain power and tilt the Republic toward a more aristocratic rule.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-outunmoor.name: Outunmoor
republic-of-freelands-outunmoor.description: Cloaked in perpetual twilight, the Outunmoor Swamp stretches across the northern Freelands, its expanse veiled in spectral fog. This marsh is home to a unique ecosystem, attracting scholars and healers with its rare herbs—both valuable and perilous to gather. Yet its true allure lies in the hidden Lakilato Ruins, where the ancient Ruins of Kölm stand as the remains of a once mighty Kemet kingdom that was abandoned ages ago. Many adventurers have sought to explore the ruins; some return bearing powerful magic items, while others vanish without a trace. Recent rumors suggest that an ancient curse has reawakened near Lakilato, leading to the mysterious disappearance of numerous explorers. This curse is believed to transform intruders into swamp monstrosities. However, the swamp is indeed fraught with danger. Numerous lizardfolk tribes inhabit the regions far from the Lakilato Ruins, and within the ruins themselves, Penumbral Rifts are concealed in sunken structures, allowing aberrations to emerge from the Penumbral Plane. On moonless nights, the ancient Kemet magic that lingers in the ruins stirs, reanimating the deceased as undead for a single night. One specific locus of power, known only to Avelum and Rigilia in the Republic, as well as Grace Sung in the Magocracy, is the Stone Circles in the northern part of Lakilato. Here, ancient magic enables portals to other planes of existence to open, provided the runed stones are correctly aligned during specific celestial events. Occasionally, extraplanar beings breach into Tanares through this nexus; some cross willingly, while others are transported without understanding their new whereabouts.
republic-of-freelands-outunmoor.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-shortfall-forest.name: Shortfall Forest
republic-of-freelands-shortfall-forest.description: The Shortfall Forest, known as the ‘Jewel of the South’ within the Republic, boasts majestic trees and verdant undergrowth. Deep within lies the abandoned lair of Huradrin, a dwarven druid who is now one of the kings of Stonelair. This hut is formed by an opening in the roots of a massive ancient tree. Its walls are etched with glowing druidic runes, leading to the underground realm of Undertanares. Lately, the tranquil forest has been overtaken by unrest. Oncepeaceful creatures are now showing aggression. Owlbears, typically reclusive, are attacking travelers on the roads. Ettercaps, previously bound to the forest’s east by druid magic, now wander to assault anyone venturing into the forest. The treants have gone into hiding, and many dryads are exhibiting symptoms of a disease with black marks, which, in its later stages, may turn them into wicked forest hags. The dryads are seeking Stoneoak, the eldest treant, a great archdruid, and Huradrin’s mentor, believing it may have answers. Rumors suggest Stoneoak may be found close to Huradrin’s lair, searching for an ancient secret in the Undertanares. Lumberjacks and rangers have started vanishing, alarming the people of Aeyefall, who depend on the forest. Desperate, they seek aid from the Adventurer’s Guild. Yet, the Eternal Circle’s druids and rangers blame Aeyefall’s inhabitants for the forest’s plight, deterring them with beasts and magic. Tensions are rising as the Circle is also clashing with the Spawners, a sect of the Cult of Shadow Wing. These cultists are erecting shrines to Droggath in hidden caverns in the forest. Their leader, “The Blighter,” a fat undead hill giant with a taste for eating the hearts of his victims, is roaming the forest. Whether they are the cause of the forest’s recent disturbances or are just seizing the opportunity to advance the sinister agenda of their dark master is uncertain.
republic-of-freelands-shortfall-forest.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-the-city-of-aeyefa.name: The City of Aeyefall
republic-of-freelands-the-city-of-aeyefa.description: Aeyefall, once Outumn’s capital, still shows traces of its oppressive past. Now, the city blends grand stone structures with newer, elegant wooden buildings, their bright roofs symbolizing the people’s spirit. Though its past splendor has faded, Aeyefall thrives with its timber and woodcraft, thanks to the nearby Shortfall Forest. Atop the city’s tallest cliff sits an eerie citadel. Formerly the home of Outumn’s Imperial Governor, it’s now a haunting reminder of dark times. Years ago, Imperial Wizards experimented on prisoners within its depths, in search to advance the methods of creating brainwashed Ironhand soldiers. These cruel trials left tormented spirits, who now roam its halls. These spirits are able to take control of dead bodies and rise as undead, making the citadel’s dungeons dangerous. While there have been attempts to exorcize them, the spirits keep returning. Protective sigils, supervised by the Celestianist Church, now seal the citadel. Yet, the Republic wizards are arguing that these ghosts may hold the last remains of knowledge about the Imperial Wizards research, which could potentially free thousands of Ironhand soldiers from the Empire’s mind control. This sparks tension between the wizards wanting research and the Church and the city watch who want to keep the citadel sealed. The Church seeks ways to purify the citadel, but what binds the spirits remains a mystery. Some think an artifact hidden in the citadel might be the cause; others feel the souls’ desire vengeance. A lasting solution eludes the clerics. Secretly, a powerful vampire, Lord Krox (NE vampire, with access to all spells of an archmage), resides in the Citadel. A formidable archmage in life, he is able to bypass the Church’s barriers, and has made the citadel his fortress. The old governor’s home is now his opulent den where he brings his victims. His intentions remain unclear, but he seems to feed only on individuals whom he sees as a disruption to Aeyefall, while his goal involves restoring the city to its former prestige for unclear reasons.
republic-of-freelands-the-city-of-aeyefa.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-the-port-city-of-g.name: The Port City of Goldraft
republic-of-freelands-the-port-city-of-g.description: Goldraft City, once a great port city of the Empire, now struggles amidst the Republic’s economic hurdles. While bronze domes and spires stretch toward the heavens, echoing past glories, the city has clearly lost its luster. During the day, one can see the enduring stalls of the merchants and the many ships docking, as people strive to make a living. Myriad sails and flags wave, each symbolizing their captain’s ambition. At the city’s heart, an ancient lighthouse emits a haunting green light, which local whispers say guides more than mere ships. Yet it is at dawn that the bustling port truly comes alive, with adventurers weaving through streets filled with diverse inns and boisterous taverns bustling with captains, merchants, buccaneers, adventurers, and locals. Their nightly festivities paint a facade of joy, immersed in ale, dice games, and loud music. Yet danger looms. A deadly plague, marked by black spots and hallucinations, spreads from the docks, sparing no one; even mighty pirate captains fall victim to it. Rumors trace its origin to a cursed island or perhaps the chants of dark cultists. Locals accuse sailors of introducing the disease, while sailors deem the city cursed. Many captains are now beginning to avoid the port of Goldraft, risking the city’s primary trade. As tensions rise, famine may soon join the plague as another impending peril. Amidst this situation, a local legend speaks of a place where a sick man can potentially find a cure: the Shadow Harbor’s Market. Stories tell of a ghostly market where souls are traded, overseen by malevolent faeries. This elusive place appears only on full moons as an inconspicuous door within one of the city’s alleys, always in a different location. Rumor says that an ancient pact binds this market to Goldraft. Still, Goldraft’s allure remains. Adventurers flock here to brave treacherous waters, pursue pirates, uncover hidden treasures, and safeguard merchant ships. Despite its challenges, Goldraft City continues to attract those eager to forge their own sagas.
republic-of-freelands-the-port-city-of-g.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-the-winterhold-cit.name: The Winterhold City
republic-of-freelands-the-winterhold-cit.description: Winterhold, a city of the winter elves, lies by the delta of the Humming Gulf. Each manor showcases the Kemet style of architecture, complete with Gothic spires and towers that overshadow ornate courtyards. Their stone facades are adorned with shadowed alcoves and intricate ironwork, making these elegant yet harrowing manors serve as fortresses for various clans. On the streets, a blend of elves and undead can be seen, with the undead performing most of the menial work in the city. At night, undead servants carrying lanterns cast ghostly glows, creating eerie shadows on the columns and turrets of surrounding buildings. The only sounds are the dragging of bony feet and the fluttering wings of crows, mixed with the waves crashing along the coast. Currently, the city is in turmoil due to mysterious murders. Dead bodies are found at night, marked with disturbing Kemet symbols. Rumors are circulating about a possible Kemet spy, winter elf clan disputes using the Kemet name as a pretext, or even a scheme of the Cult of Shadow Wing. Compounding the unease, some undead have begun showing signs of defiance, alarming the city’s nobility. The noble houses are seeking aid to investigate these issues, but so far, they remain unresolved. Another problem is a political struggle against the conservatives in the Republic’s parliament. A decade ago, it became common for winter elves to pay for the right to animate a person’s body as a mindless undead after death, a practice necessary to maintain their number of servants. They assert that the soul of the deceased is free to journey into the afterlife; however, many in the Republic are apprehensive about this practice, raising concerns about potential assassinations, exploitation of the impoverished, and violations of sacred burial rites. The winter elves argue that a body is merely an object, and that individuals have the right to sell their bodies post-mortem. With the looming threat of Kemet naval forces, lawmakers on both sides are desperate to find common ground, understanding that this issue must not fracture their unity.
republic-of-freelands-the-winterhold-cit.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

republic-of-freelands-yellow-creek.name: Yellow Creek
republic-of-freelands-yellow-creek.description: Crossing the northern woodlands of the Republic is the Yellow Creek, renowned for its unique yellow-hued waters. Though curiously tinted, its waters are drinkable, immune to corruption, and impervious to diseases, curses, and poisons. This anomaly attracts alchemists, who attempt to harness its essence for potion-making. Local tales attribute the creek’s color to a great wizard, hunted by the Empire and slain by her lover, who had been transformed into a mindless Ironhand soldier. Her demise near the creek infused its waters with her golden life essence. Her ghostly image is rumored to dance atop the water during full moons. Some of the tales continue by claiming that she was not only a wizard but a demigod from another plane, arriving in Tanares to pursue aboleths that fled her hunt. She fell in love with a human, but tragically, her love story was manipulated by the aboleths, leading to her death and the creek’s divine tint. Yet, beyond legend, it is true that the creek stands as a barrier against a hidden aboleth colony in the forest’s southern region. These malevolent beings shun the creek’s waters, making the creek a natural shield for neighboring settlements, thus being the source of the myths about it. At the colony’s leadership is Abyllisoth, an ancient aboleth from the wizard’s plane, his arrival predating even the Ungods. Distinct from typical Aboleths who side with the Ungods, Abyllisoth loathes both sides of the divine conflict, aiming to obliterate all deities in Tanares. Unlike his cruel kin, Abyllisoth is calculating and subtle, favoring strategic manipulation and keeping his existence hidden. His colony does not attack land residents if not with a clear purpose. His endgame is to amass mystical power in the form of artifacts and knowledge, positioning himself for the inevitable final clash between gods and Ungods that he plans to manipulate, ensuring both sides are destroyed. As part of his strategy, he employs marsh goblins and kua-toas, gathering all sorts of magic items to ready himself for the day Tanares falls to his kind.
republic-of-freelands-yellow-creek.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

seashores-bluhaven-the-capital.name: Bluhaven, the Capital
seashores-bluhaven-the-capital.description: At first glance, the capital of Seashores disappoints. Most of it is very disorganized, with many piers and docks full of poor taverns but full of people. As the Parliament is absent, the city serves as the primary gathering point for pirates and all sorts of outlaws who conduct their activities here completely unchecked. Taverns here are notorious for brawls, arguments, illicit dealings, and meeting spots for hiring equally dirty services. Except for those under the Parliament’s protection, whom no pirate dares to disturb, the city remains a dangerous place for many. Many shipyards are located here, usually heavily secured, and many places for trading sea goods and weapons, stolen items, and even ships. The regent, William the Whale, titled for his size, allows most types of crime as long he gets some profit. When someone commits a grave crime, he applies a particularly disturbing sentence. In the center square, people can throw stones and lances at the criminal, but when the person is almost dying, a cleric heals the wounds, and the punishment continues. Here is a place where many adventurers are hired, some to protect people, some to eliminate inconvenient persons, and some to steal important items.
seashores-bluhaven-the-capital.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

seashores-mustardseed.name: Mustardseed
seashores-mustardseed.description: The most majestic and sophisticated city in Tanares, Mustardseed is a place of art and knowledge. Divided into thematic districts based on the other nations of Tanares, it is filled with places showcasing art and architecture to symbolize many aspects of the theme. Some are comical, illustrating the caricatural features of other nations, especially notable people. Many animated instruments create melodic streets, which are also thematic. The residences seem to defy physics, are sophisticated and adorned with beautiful paintings and magic items that enhance the beauty of household utensils. Their society values the individual for their education, manners, and etiquette. As a result, many unnecessary formalities arise when speaking to a gnome. The city’s crown jewel is the ‘Academy of Light,’ dedicated to deep studies in art, knowledge, and music. Despite its appearance of safety, the city harbors dangers. The city houses stone guards that can cast a secret spell to trap a person in a painting, an evil and cunning opera singer with the power to enrage non-gnomes, violent etiquette enforcers patrolling the streets, and many eccentric individuals seeking outlets for their frustrations. As lovers of sound, constant music fills the air, conveying messages when necessary. Much like the music, their artworks contain subliminal messages that often go entirely unnoticed. They boast the largest and most highly regarded music schools, The Academies of Light, which can also be found in every corner of Tanares. Closely tied to their past, in their constant quest to revive their culture and tradition, they are always organizing expeditions into the depths of the Central Sea in search of their relics and artifacts. However, there are numerous challenges, ranging from dealing with lizardfolk who have taken over some of the submerged caves to navigating the labyrinth formed by the rocks and structures that were once part of their kingdom. Occasionally, they receive assistance from the Merfolks, but most of the time, they rely on contracted groups.

seashores-pearl-town.name: Pearl Town
seashores-pearl-town.description: It is a beautiful underwater city built by the merfolks, filled with magic that allows people to breathe underwater. Accessible through a small island, it is heavily guarded by merfolks and water elementals. The city is a center for trade for the merfolks, who usually ask for favors instead of gold for their valuable goods. Underwater, the city can release many unusual defense mechanisms, like water currents, jellyfish swarms, black ink curtains, and others. It is ruled by the merfolk queen Zhelahra, the greatest sorcery among them, usually changing her appearance to a blue elf when dealing with humans. She is kind and benevolent, using her melody to calm rough waters and help the lost sailors find their way. Like a siren’s song, her voice is revered as the most beautiful, and it is hard to resist falling in love with her chant. She has three major concerns: the cursed sunken city, spawning undead merfolks and other aquatic creatures; the corrupted coral reef near the abyssal regions, which emits a dark light that maddens the merfolk; and the increased number of pirate slavers, who sell the merfolks as pets for wealthy nobles from distant lands. She is always willing to reward fairly and share her vast information about the sea mysteries.

seashores-the-whirlpool.name: The Whirlpool
seashores-the-whirlpool.description: This immense and constantly powerful tidal wave has existed since the first formation of the Central Sea itself. Occupying part of the southern region of Seashores, it compels vessels to take alternative routes through treacherous, rock-laden passages. It is also the Parliament’s chosen site for executing prisoners: they are made to walk the plank and jump into the whirlpool, surviving only as long as they can swim before exhaustion claims them. Some sages believe this whirlpool connects with a water-related plane and others with Undertanares, justifying the rivers and lakes there. Having claimed many ships in the past, exploring it could lead to discoveries beyond imagination, if the adventurer is prepared to breathe in water and resist its pressure.
seashores-the-whirlpool.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

seashores-uncle-joe-s-tavern.name: Uncle Joe’s Tavern
seashores-uncle-joe-s-tavern.description: If one were to pinpoint the center of black market trade, it would be Uncle Joe’s tavern. There, it is possible to find a variety of unique items, typically offered by members of factions such as the Third Eye, Bloodbound, and The Dragon Syndicate. Located on a small island of the Fire Archipelago, it is a meeting place not just for pirates, but also for many members of various organizations. It is forbidden to fight inside the island, especially in the tavern and its luxurious inn. Uncle Joe, a retired and good-humored pirate, enjoys brokering deals over a hearty banquet. He deals in magic items and vessels, buying, selling, or even renting them, meticulously recording all transactions and basic customer information. The island is heavily guarded by creatures such as ogres, giants, and kobolds, as well as beings summoned by his artifacts, like rakshasas and other strange entities.

seashores-underwater-dungeon.name: Underwater dungeon
seashores-underwater-dungeon.description: Legends tell about a vast, labyrinthine dungeon in the north Central Sea. It is filled with luminescent flora and fauna and some breathable chambers. This is where remnants from battles against the Ungods rest, so very unique relics can be found there, especially the penumbral stone, a gem with powers that supposedly match the moonstone. The stories narrate a hero who had to open the doors by redirecting the water current there when activating a water device, passing through coral labyrinths, facing sea monstrosities, including giant piranhas, and traps where touching the wrong combination of stones causes the water to boil. In the tale, he discovers an ancient library and a mysterious box. The end of the story was lost in time, but people say this hero became a guardian of the place.

sindile-forest-cindergrove.name: Cindergrove
sindile-forest-cindergrove.description: Spring elves are gifted a seed when young to carry for their whole lives. When it dies, the seed is planted here to become one of the trees of Cindergrove. The trees sprouted in this manner carry the essence of the elf, allowing its memories to endure and offering guidance to others. This grove is beautiful, with colorful flowers and butterflies contrasting with the grey-bark trees that give the place its name. A significant part of it was destroyed by orc raiders long ago, leaving part of the location barren as some ancient stone obelisks carved with druidic magic were damaged as the orcs pilled their emerald cores. To this day, the elves search for these stones, as each obelisk recovered means another section of Cindergrove that will be able to grow again. The elves value this location not only for its natural importance but also because of the memories it stores. Touching one of the trees can allow one to talk with the essence of an ancient elf, who can even impart memories to the living. Some of them have unfinished business and may ask for help; others have long goals and still try to convince others to take their mantle. Their rewards are intriguing; they impart knowledge into the person’s mind for a time, often between one day and a few weeks. However, rumors say that some powerful deceased elves can grant much more durable, or even permanent, powers. Many elves have even been trained by these essences as their masters, touching the trees every day to commune with them and receive wisdom for their daily practices, emerging as powerful heroes after long seclusion. Elven Essence Boon. The elven essence can grant specific memories, proficiency with a tool, language, skills, or even one or more class features from that elf’s past (of GM choice). Still, the memory or knowledge disappears entirely after a set amount of time. It is said that the elves visit Cindergrove when they know of an invasion to gain extraordinary abilities to defend their forest, which is one of the secrets of why they were never overtaken.
sindile-forest-cindergrove.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

sindile-forest-hunter-s-nest.name: Hunter’s Nest
sindile-forest-hunter-s-nest.description: Miles away from Sweetsprings lies the fortified and warlike elven construction known as Hunter’s Nest. Here, the majority of their warriors gather with their vast arsenal, most created from breithwood, including a collection of magical bows and arrows. Unlike their capital, this city stands on the ground level. The constructions are practical and military-oriented but still contain beautiful elven architecture. Rigorous training and strategic planning sessions frequently occur here, preparing the elves to defend Sindile Forest and even explore its depths. Niary, the renowned elven heroine, leads the training and is very rigorous, because she hates incompetence. At the slightest sign of flaws, she complains and applies some punishment to encourage her warriors to be perfect. It is severe training but very effective. Each spring, she promotes the archery contest on neutral ground, inviting foreigners to the event. The last champions were two humans, whom Niary accepted as her students. Recently, the last group of elite soldiers was sent into the forest. However, only a few returned alive, and they were suffering from a form of memory loss, rendering them unable to report the facts. She sent the word to Sedura to find competent and trustworthy adventurers to investigate the matter, as she must continue protecting the cities.
sindile-forest-hunter-s-nest.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

sindile-forest-mirror-lake.name: Mirror Lake
sindile-forest-mirror-lake.description: In the heart of Sindile, within the Mountain Gate temples region, lies the location where the elves first arrived in Tanares. Mirror Lake, blessed by Breith, the Lord of Spring, showcases a stunningly reflective surface that once served as the portal to the elven dying world. It is a sacred place from where elven druids draw water to cleanse the Mother Trees during their purification rituals. Guarded by the heroic nymph Thalia, this lake holds immense sanctity for the Spring Elves and is one of Sindile’s most awe-inspiring locations. The Mirror Lake reflects the expansive gardens, meticulously tended by Thalia, other nymphs, and select archdruids, displaying a vibrant array of enchanted roses of many different colors. Each rose, believed to possess curative properties for various ailments, curses, and penumbral corruption, draws many to the druids for healing. However, Breith stipulates that seekers of the lake’s water or flowers be swiftly aided but then bound by an oath to undertake a task decreed by the god, tailored to the individual’s capabilities, invariably aimed at combating world corruption. The lake’s significance makes it a target for the Cult of Shadow Wing, who seek to corrupt it. Thus, elves, druids, and nymphs remain on high alert, often enlisting adventurers and heroes to thwart the Cult’s schemes. Such tasks may involve venturing beyond the forest to counteract the Cult’s insidious activities in Undertanares or their efforts in the penumbral plane to open a rift in Sindile and unleash an army against the lake. Devotees of Breith and believers in the World Spirits frequent this site, drawn by its unparalleled natural energy. Natural Energy. Within this place, all druid and ranger spells have their duration doubled and gain +2 to their spell DCs and attack rolls, as one can gather much greater natural power here than anywhere else in Tanares. Elves, halflings, and other species inherently tied to nature’s energy who make a long here gain 2 temporary hit points per level, lasting until they rest long. Rose Powers. The roses of Mirror Lake, when distilled into potions, yield powerful remedies. sindile-forest-sindile-road.name: Sindile Road
sindile-forest-sindile-road.description: After much controversy surrounding the construction of a road after the Kemet Invasion, the king finally ordered its creation. Connecting Yama, Mystical, and Tsvetan, the road was built with the aid of Earth Elementals, ensuring no tree will cover it. This road only skirts the periphery of Sindile and does not penetrate its depths. Some magical mosses and fungi provide some illumination by night, and earth elementals act as silent guides, helping travelers navigate the pathway. This road also magically erases any footprints, making it impossible to track. The Eternal Circle periodically makes some sabotages, creating dangers on the road or guiding people to strange places, even to the depths of the forest. They officially deny such actions, the more formidable the group crossing the road, the more probable they are to draw their attention. A few elven small villages can be found across the road, and even with restrictions, they can trade or offer guidance.
sindile-forest-sindile-road.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

sindile-forest-sweetsprings.name: Sweetsprings
sindile-forest-sweetsprings.description: Untouched and majestic is the common definition of the capital of the spring elves in Sindile by foreign visitors. Divided into levels, its floors are like rings surrounding the colossal tree trunks, interconnected by bridges or elevators. Its construction is so complex that it blends with the very branches and leaves of the trees to the point that a distracted traveler on the ground may not even realize the presence of the city. They use equipment crafted from breithwood to transport themselves and goods through the levels, some methods very curious. Only the Council, priests and elementalists are allowed to access the upper levels, where the sunlight reaches the city more intensively. The Council of Guardians meets with the king and queen in a fancy hall called Breith’s cocoon, which is sacred to them. Foreigners are typically confined to the city’s lower levels, under strong vigilance. There have been heated debates since Sedura was invited into the structure, as many believe she would destroy the purity of the place. To make things worse, one of the trees died soon after, fueling debates about desecration. Some guardians believe that was an action by the Eternal Circle, but could not confirm. The king often speaks slowly and explains things to foreigners as though he’s speaking to children, so any meeting with him requires extra patience and diplomacy.
sindile-forest-sweetsprings.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

sindile-forest-verdant-colossus.name: Verdant Colossus
sindile-forest-verdant-colossus.description: In Tanares, the largest tree is not one of the colossal Mother Trees but an even larger sequoia. This tree, now a living fortress, was cultivated by Vollanas Deepleaf, one of the druid hierophants who led the crossing from their home plane to Tanares. He endeavored to bring many relics from his world to their new home, but after arriving, humans stole some of his sacred items. The loss of his world and the ancient artifacts he had sworn to protect caused Vollanas to lose his sanity, and he became obsessed with securing the relics from his world. He transformed the giant tree in the forest into his fortress to protect the remaining relics, creating a dungeon with multiple levels extending underground within its roots and branches. It is said to hold ancient elven relics and the possessions of many who dared to explore its depths and never returned. The dungeon has labyrinths of wooden passages and enchanted leaf walls. Those who perish within are transformed into plant-like guardians, eternally defending the tree. Rumors suggest a portal within it leads to the elven homeworld, now a frozen, lifeless expanse. Hierophant Bennalas forbade entry into the tree, but the few who defied him died or were forced to flee. In a scandalously kept secret, the king’s only son ventured into the tree to prove his courage but never returned. The queen, acting discreetly, has since offered rewards to adventurers who search for him, always choosing foreigners and maintaining her anonymity to avoid public attention. The Plant Guardians. It retains its original stats, but its type changes to Plant. It gains resistance to bludgeoning and piercing damage, vulnerability to fire damage, its speed is reduced by 5 ft. (to a minimum of 5 ft.), and it gains a natural armor bonus of +2 to AC.
