sindile-forest-verdant-expanse-of-yrthak.name: Verdant Expanse of Yrthak
sindile-forest-verdant-expanse-of-yrthak.description: In the depths of Sindile Forest lies a portal to Yrthak, a plane of existence unfathomable to ordinary travelers. Those who cross the portal find themselves in a dense, sweltering jungle where the air is heavy with humidity and filled with the constant noise of exotic birds. This world, largely uncharted by the Tanareans, is viewed by scholars and explorers alike as a blend of danger and wonder. The jungle of Yrthak is home to a myriad of lizard creatures, ranging from aquatic plesiosaurs to herds of triceratops and from the terrifying tyrannosaurs that hunt the wilderness to the Primedraconids - enormous, bestial draconic creatures that fly over the forest, hunting purely by instinct, always hungry. Amidst this savage splendor, ancient temples lie hidden in the forest. Harboring the secrets of the gods they honor and magical artifacts of untold power, these stone structures were erected by a unique species of lizardfolk inhabiting Yrthak. While some temples are old and abandoned, filled with traps, and protected by sorcery, others are actively used for sacred rites. The lizardfolk in the region the Tanareans explored so far can be divided into three groups. The Servants of Azskah. Calm and tradition-bound, these lizardfolk are the self-appointed guardians of Yrthak. They worship Azskah, a colossal winged serpent revered as the creator of their world. Their society, structured and adhering to strict traditional laws, fervently opposes any external intrusion, especially from the Tanareans, fearing they will bring the corruption of the Ungods. In their eyes, every outsider is a potential harbinger of desecration. Despite their desire to seal off their realm, the secrets to close the portal elude them. Distinguished by their use of feathers as indumentary, with colors signifying their societal roles, they are led by High Priests who answer to the Azskahnian King, a leader empowered by their serpent deity. Azskah, a god of healing, protection, and vengeance, instills in his followers the importance of life, mutual protection, and retribution for those who harm them. This often leads them to make incursions against the Spawns of Ukka for hunting Azskahnians. The temples of Azskah are rumored to contain untold riches, magical items that can rejuvenate individuals, and even scales said to be from Azskah himself, capable of reviving the dead. The Spawns of Ukka. Warriors of raw, untamed ferocity, these lizardfolk live by the hunt. In the dense undergrowth, they pursue their prey with a zeal bordering on fanaticism. Devotees of Ukka, the Scaled Sorceress, they believe her to be the first of their species, the mother of all, and the giver of all magic. They sacrifice non-believing lizardfolk to return their spirits to “Greatmother Ukka,” allowing them to be reborn from their eggs as purified believers. Sacrificial rituals are also made using powerful hunted creatures or Tanarean explorers, demonstrating Ukka’s power. They hunt Azskahnians and Jungle Walkers, believing those who stray from Ukka are misguided. They particularly detest Azskah and its priests, seeing their deity as a devilish snake attempting to steal Ukka’s offspring, just as snakes sneak on their eggs. While the Ukkanians may hunt explorers in Yrthak, they sometimes strike deals with adventurers, trading information and the locations of Azskah’s secret temples in exchange for help eliminating more of the serpent deity’s servants. The Jungle Walkers. These nomadic druids embody the spirit of Yrthak’s wilderness. Harmonizing with nature, they roam the jungle as a nomadic society, collecting and hunting as necessary while blending with the fantastic nature around them. Unlike their kin, they welcome outsiders, viewing the looming threat of the Ungods as a universal peril that will endanger their world if not addressed. They see the Servants of Azskah as overly rigid and the Spawns of Ukka as corrupted, deviating from the natural balance they cherish. Open to trade with explorers and adventurers, they generally respect Azskahnians and are often in search of aid to rescue captured Walkers destined for sacrifice to Ukka. Adventurers venturing into Yrthak are drawn into a world where the allure of ancient mysteries and a constant struggle for dominance create a perpetual survival challenge. The jungle, teeming with dangerous creatures, cursed temples, and hunting lizardfolk, offers dangers and opportunities for those brave enough to explore this uncharted world. storm-islands-cantala-ruins.name: Cantala Ruins
storm-islands-cantala-ruins.description: Many caves in Storm Island are passages to an ancient dungeon. It is the Lost City of Cantala, filled with mazes, secret chambers, and even an underground forest sustained by a strange spell that keeps the trees alive. Historically, the inhabitants were renowned for their knowledge of astronomy and their unique star spells. The kemets have already found some papers containing a few of their spells, but they are still studying how to use these instructions. At every entrance to the dungeon stands an indestructible statue of a woman holding a star and the name Amarila at its base. Recently, all these statues began to shed tears for unknown reasons. It is not easy to reach this place since it’s located within the heart of the Storm Islands, but many adventurers dream of the powerful relics that can be found there.

storm-islands-dark-lab.name: Dark Lab
storm-islands-dark-lab.description: Numerous kemet warriors, necromancers, and undead guard this subterranean facility, located near Night Mansions. This is where they conduct experiments to develop new types of undead. It has many chambers and testing fields, with cages and prisons where they confine both the created undead and subjects for experimentation. The central chamber is the reanimation atrium, where the main tests are performed. There are also pits, with giant caldrons filled with bubbling green liquid. Many incubators, bone depots, and processors for failed experiments can be found everywhere. Kemets commonly capture creatures from various species for their experiments. After the transformation, the Kemets usually teleport the experiments to specific locations to be tested or lock them in prison. These creatures maintain their intelligence and memories for one week, after which they fall completely under kemet control. Reversion is possible in the Dark Lab, on a specific incubator. storm-islands-night-mansions.name: Night Mansions
storm-islands-night-mansions.description: Unlike other regions, the Kemets of Storm Islands have a singular urban concentration known as Night Mansions. In a valley surrounded by walls of ice, mists, and frost, a vast assemblage of palaces and grand mansions lies. Every architectural detail meticulously emphasizes death, adorned with skulls, bones, and numerous sharp and macabre ornaments. The skeletons and zombies handle the hard work, allowing the citizens to devote themselves to Bás and train in combat, ice elementalism, and necromancy. Entire families, including extended relatives, commonly inhabit these mansions, attended to by undead servants. During the Midnight Sun, many events take place throughout the city. Magical musical instruments play, undead battle in the Arena of the Undead, and numerous other festivities occur. A law of the city dictates that no one may attack another within its boundaries. Offenders face severe punishment, typically lashing by ice whips. The cumulative slashes deal a total of 5d6 damage, and the wounded creature cannot regain hit points until finishing a long rest. When foreigners visit the city, some kemets provoke them solely to relish the spectacle of their punishment.
storm-islands-night-mansions.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

storm-islands-shrine-of-bas.name: Shrine of Bás
storm-islands-shrine-of-bas.description: Each shrine dedicated to this god is imbued with elements of death and ice, both inside and out. The exterior has some statues of kemets carrying torches of cold blue flame. An enormous pylon made of tameranium floats above the shrine, emanating intense cold energy that creates the Deep Freeze zone. Many structures on the interior are made of pure ice, such as the altar, chalice, and even statues. Some frozen tombs with the bodies of traitors are displayed there. Typically, the shrine is attended by at least three priests of Bás, alongside some experienced warriors, and undead to secure the place. If invaded, the shrine’s defenders can manipulate the cold and unleash the traitors, reanimated as frosty undead. The Pylon becomes exposed and can be destroyed (100 hit points, AC 15, damage threshold 15) if the central altar is ruined.
storm-islands-shrine-of-bas.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

storm-islands-thyra-cave.name: Thyra Cave
storm-islands-thyra-cave.description: Kemet necromancers are developing an advanced technique to reanimate undead dragons. They take the bodies of these creatures to the Dark Lab to experiment and create powerful undead from their remains. They are now trying to locate Thyra’s hideout on a secret island within Storm Island territory. If they can reanimate an avatar dragon, the devastation it might bring could be catastrophic. Some agents of the Draconic Council are recruiting adventurers to find this location before the kemet does, to remove her body, in case she is really dead. Adventurers might not only discover her body but also her unimaginable treasures and dragon eggs. Solnertha has an even more ambitious dream. She learned that the body of a dead Ungod lies in the central sea. If it could be reanimated, maybe the Kemet could annihilate all enemies using this monster.
storm-islands-thyra-cave.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

stravian-domains-dorsian-forge.name: Dorsian Forge
stravian-domains-dorsian-forge.description: Hidden in Undertanares, the Dorsian Forge is the best achievement of the ancient dwarves. It is the mightiest forge on the Material Plane, designed to craft weapons formidable enough to counter the Ungods’ invasion. It consists of multiple smaller forges, with each one handling different aspects of item creation, such as magma and ice forges, and can be combined into one colossal single forge using an activation mechanism. It can forge any magic item or unique artifact as long as the blacksmith possesses detailed instructions and components for its creation. It also can combine tameranium and bauronite to create moonstone, the rarest and most powerful mineral. It even has the capability to transform base materials, such as iron, into precious metals like adamantine or mithral. Weapons forged here gain a unique ability, which may vary based on the forging process. The most common is the accurate burst, granting advantage for one attack roll once per hour, or memory metal, containing memories of their last wielder. The duergar control the forge, but they have not yet been able to activate the combined forge. Even utilizing its basic capabilities, they can craft formidable weapons. Additionally, Drogolin discovered a metallic statue shaped like a dwarf. His priests have found the means to create the Iron Spirits using the soul of Skrabolin. If the duergars learn how to mass-produce these statues, their army will be much more powerful. As expected, the dwarves pay large sums of gold for anyone capable of reclaiming this forge.

stravian-domains-eclipse-village.name: Eclipse Village
stravian-domains-eclipse-village.description: This village serves as a refuge for many bandits, salters, and mercenaries hiding from authorities. The village is centered around Main Street, featuring wooden and stone structures such as saloons, inns, general stores, blacksmiths, stables, and dueling grounds. The rest of the village has modest wooden homes and ranches. It is a no man’s land with no security or government; the only authority is the bandit master, Kibral, considered the quickest crossbowman in the Stravian West. They typically ride horses that are magically empowered to run faster and longer. These bandits attack caravans and travelers using crossbows and explosive arcane barrels. In the village, bards play at the saloons using unique instruments recovered from ruins. Many disagreements are resolved with a crossbow duel, some ending in death. Kibral is a formidable combatant and can use his crossbow much faster than most, shooting four bolts in the time it usually takes to shoot one. He cares more for glory and the role of a boss, or sheriff as he calls himself, than the gold and items stolen. Kibral is considered the most wanted criminal in Stravian, so many adventurers are hired to arrest or kill him. None succeeded until now.
stravian-domains-eclipse-village.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

stravian-domains-malland-hing-halls.name: Malland Hing Halls
stravian-domains-malland-hing-halls.description: Close to the city of Stonelair stands a monolith alongside an entrance to a vast dungeon. It takes at least a day’s journey on foot to traverse it. These are the Malland King Halls. Unfortunately, it is protected by a magic barrier that is impossible to break, even using the most powerful known spells. After a long study, the dwarf sages believe they need someone with the descendency of Malrok to cross the barrier; they are now searching for a courageous individual with the Ancient Blood. They offer rewards for any information leading to such an individual. The scholars suggest this place is both a prison and a treasure hall. Malrok kept powerful extraplanar beings and other dangerous entities locked away, beings he could not destroy. However, it contains artifacts from his Age that Malrok considered powerful enough to keep hidden.
stravian-domains-malland-hing-halls.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

stravian-domains-mirare.name: Mirare
stravian-domains-mirare.description: Located along the shores of the Central Sea, the city is the largest and most renowned halfling community in Tanares. With the blessing of Fruitful, this place is considered the granary of Tanares, with abundant food production. The city is full of small houses for the halflings, but there is a separate district for foreigners with regularly sized houses. There is an unusual number of taverns and central squares. Even the beach has structures to be a place of entertainment. Its mayor, Aldo Cotton-Hair, constantly promotes festivities and games in the name of the feys. During some of them, it’s common for the wealthiest halflings to bring some giant fruits produced by feys’ magic to share. The larger and more imposing the fruit brought, the more prestige and status the halfling gains. Some common games: Fruit-eating. Competitors must eat the most fruits in five minutes. Each must make Constitution 15 saving throws to avoid getting full or sick. The number of successful saves in a row determines the winner, but each test increases the difficulty by 2. Fruit Dish Race. A race with a twist. Competitors must balance a dish of fruits. If any of them drops, it must restart the racing. Dexterity (Acrobatics) 15 checks to maintain balance. Failed checks result in dropping fruits. For those who succeeded, a Strength check and compare the results to determine the winner. Story Narration. The competitor who tells the most captivating story wins. First, it must make an DC 15 Intelligence check to think of good elements. Then, make a Charisma (Performance) check, having advantage in case of a successful Intelligence check. The winner is the competitor who gets the biggest number in the last test.
stravian-domains-mirare.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

stravian-domains-moolooite-mines.name: Moolooite Mines
stravian-domains-moolooite-mines.description: This ghost mine is one of the places the dwarves avoid the most. All of its workers died tragically and were cursed to remain within the mines indefinitely. In the Ethereal Plane, they have established a village inside and continue to mine ores that are unique to that plane. They also have a forge there and create ethereal weapons and armor. On the Material Plane, these ethereal items cannot be obtained. However, it has caught the interest of certain necromancers who frequently traverse that plane and some priests from the Kepesh, who aim to use the ethereal ores for their spells and to construct the Eternal City for their deity Ba-Ka. Though it is sealed and difficult to access, some adventurers are still hired to explore it, as the dwarves believe this mine has many valuable metals.
stravian-domains-moolooite-mines.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

stravian-domains-stonelair-city.name: Stonelair City
stravian-domains-stonelair-city.description: Stonelair City is located between the Malland Range’s foothills and the Crystal Torrent cascades. Towering stone walls protect the inhabitants, and within the city lie advanced structures, such as stone elevators and suspended tombs, which are not seen anywhere else. Smoke rises from countless forges, and the rhythmic clang of hammers echoes, capturing the city’s enduring spirit. The city has a grand entrance to Undertanares, where there is a constant flow of people and mining carts. The city is governed by the three Dwarven Kings—Rurik, Huradrin, and Ukhumlin—who extend opportunities for all to prosper, opening their rich mines for collective exploration. Known for its masonry, forging, trade, and jewel crafting, the city thrives on hard work, with its inhabitants taking only brief moments of rest. The city has another part inside the Undertanares with many distinguished features. The cleric class receives new subclasses in this section.
stravian-domains-stonelair-city.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

taii-maku-city-states-awo-irin-illu.name: Awo Irin Illu
taii-maku-city-states-awo-irin-illu.description: This city is known for innovation and has striking silver spires that shine in the sun. Its architecture combines geometric precision with functional elegance. The council here focuses on actionable plans rather than theories. Its people are practical, inclined toward engineering rather than philosophy, and favor combat training over sports and goods-producing and guard-duty golems rather than those that provide daily life amenities. Awo Irin is the most active city in reaching out to other species. They send emissaries carrying the city’s inventions rather than waiting for others to seek them. They actively pursue to shape the world according to their vision of the greater good. Most people in Awo Irin adhere to a philosophy of ethereal pragmatism, preferring to see results over intangible morals. T’ssir, who was born here, is part of the council and is currently discussing his view on blending individuals with magic and machines. Many still need to be convinced about the risks and advantages of this approach. The first tower of the Aetheric Synthesis Guild is located here, and it is from there that T’ssir exerts his influence over Tanares. Recently, several researchers and council members have died in what appear to be natural deaths, but the timing of these deaths is strange. Some believe these are coincidences, while others accuse the Cult of Shadow Wing, the Third Eye, or the Eldritch Hand. A few even point fingers at T’ssir, causing a great commotion, as such accusations are uncommon among taii’makus.
taii-maku-city-states-awo-irin-illu.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

taii-maku-city-states-g-bagede-illu.name: G’bagede Illu
taii-maku-city-states-g-bagede-illu.description: G’bagede is a city known as the City of Golems. It is famous for the high numbers of golems patrolling the streets, which are produced to safeguard the city and care for all its citizens’ daily needs. Most taii’makus here spend their days in contemplation and ethical debates, most adhering to ethical harmonism, while the golems care for their every need. The only people who work in G’bagede are teachers who educate the young and the golem researchers who develop more advanced and unique creations, aiming to have a specific golem to fill each function society needs. The Illu’s high external walls and hexagonal stone structures proudly demonstrate its culture of resilience and righteousness. Furthermore, due to their golem production, it is one of the most dedicated mining Illus, always searching for metals, especially bauronite and rare ores, with numerous golems devoted to this task. G’bagede is home to the Righteous Sun Celestianist Temple of Tamera, which preaches Tamera as a cosmic being who exemplifies virtuous conduct. It is also known to produce most of the taii’maku clerics and paladins. M’Bollo, the Wharfugee Hero, is the current bishop of this temple and a member of the council that runs the Illu. However, shipments of rare ores from Stravian have recently been targeted by pirates in the Central Seas, disrupting the flow of mithral and tameranium necessary for researching golem improvements. The city seeks help from those who can venture into the Seashores and find more. M’Bollo believes there is more behind the situation than just pirates.
taii-maku-city-states-g-bagede-illu.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

taii-maku-city-states-ilaorun-illu.name: Ilaorun Illu
taii-maku-city-states-ilaorun-illu.description: Renowned for its beautiful open gardens, the city features buildings with unique architecture, reflecting its designer’s perspective and forming a patchwork of styles. Its streets, lined with statues, complement the walls with beautiful paintings and frescoes. These artworks are not expressions of emotions but rather profound rational critiques and complex expressions of ideas made into art objects. The city council is composed of inventors, artists, and philosophers. While always open to new ideas, they are critical of any attempts to curb freedoms, create norms, or stifle innovation. However, they view personal responsibility as critical, with individuals needing to solve any damage caused by their actions. The ethos of Ilaorun Illu is to explore talents and articulate one’s unique viewpoints, spurring groundbreaking inventions, even at the cost of efficiency. For them, creativity and new connections of ideas are more valuable than material production. Most of its citizens are adepts of essential existentialism and often gather in public places to discuss their latest works and perspectives. They delve into magic and engineering to satisfy their preferences, display unique ideas, solve their personal problems, and not think about social use. The city’s workshops are filled with incredible inventions, and while some argue many are niche or inefficient, Ilaorun has also produced highly significant innovations. Ilaorun Illu is also a sanctuary for refugees fleeing tyranny, particularly scholars and artists. Here, they can contribute their thinking to the taii’maku discussions and are treated as equals. Often, revolutionaries and fugitive scholars seek the help of adventurers or mercenaries to scout them to Ilaorun and help them get accepted into it by the taii’makus. Currently, the council is divided in their discussion about T’ssir’s ideas. Some argue for freedom of research, as he is testing his theories on himself and taking responsibility. In contrast, others say his experiments turn one away from their essence and risk creating a fear of obsolescence in all those who do not accept it, and will ultimately force everyone to accept being transformed. Some counselors are secretly funding adventuring groups to investigate T’ssir and his guild to ensure they divulge all the risks.
taii-maku-city-states-ilaorun-illu.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

taii-maku-city-states-ubellian-fire-pits.name: Ubellian Fire Pits
taii-maku-city-states-ubellian-fire-pits.description: One of Tanares’ most treacherous lands, it is a scorching realm of fiery pits and lava rivers and home to several red dragons, including the mighty Avatar Dragon Azymor. The region hosts a noteworthy Dragon Tower, defended by many young dragonborns and dragonblades, as its harsh and isolated environment creates an ideal setting for training recruits. Taii’makus have a good relationship with the tower, and Azymor does not interfere with their traveling. However, other foreigners are not as well received unless they have good standards with the Draconic Council. The Shadow Lords, a sect of the Cult of Shadow Wing, have constantly attacked dragons living here, capturing living individuals and eggs to corrupt them into maddened penumbral dragons. A few penumbral dragons and their servants have taken over some caverns on the western side of the Fire Pits, becoming a threat in the region. Unknown to anyone, the one behind this strategy is Lypoec, who is trying to lure Azymor into an open battle so he can try to take down the Red Avatar Dragon. The Draconic Tower is seeking support from adventurers but is wary of accepting anyone, as the cult is always trying to infiltrate their ranks.
taii-maku-city-states-ubellian-fire-pits.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

theocracy-of-kepesh-bright-coast.name: Bright Coast
theocracy-of-kepesh-bright-coast.description: The coastline along the Storm Sea is rocky and rugged, with countless ships being claimed by its turbulent waters, sinking along their treasures. While drawing adventurers and treasure hunters, colonization here is scarce, limited to a few fishing villages. Legends about the spirits of the drowned and sea monsters give this region a cursed reputation. Kalistessenâmun’s forces know the coast is vulnerable, leaving an opening for the Kemets. Still, with a scarcity of warships and a coastline fraught with danger, the Kepesh often relies on hiring corsairs, Kolbjörn mercenaries, or adventurers for defense and patrol, an expensive necessity. The Kepesh rarely navigate the Storm Sea, as their vessels cannot match the heavily armored Kemet ships transporting undead hordes. The Kemets use their naval superiority to infiltrate the expansive coast, sending their undead and warbands to wreak havoc in the Theocracy territory with incursions that challenge the Pharaoh’s sovereignty and incite Kalistessenâmun’s wrath. Beneath certain coastal areas, extensive coral forests are guarded by merfolk. These bastions of marine life are the stages of conflict as the merfolks clash with the Samudara barbarians and defend against the Kemets, who seek to turn merfolk warriors into undead minions. The Samudara barbarians, adorned in fish leather and coral, are nocturnal raiders aboard their rudimentary boats, adding to the region’s woes. Known for their excellent swimming skills and the ability to hold their breath for long periods, they live as nomadic navigators plundering coastal villages, merfolk cities and any ship that crosses their path. They often attack Kepesh coastal villages and the Kemet ships. But what is behind them is what is truly scary. Deep within the Storm Sea’s caverns dwells a powerful Kraken and its offspring. The Samudara appease this leviathan with offerings and serve its unknowable will. The Kraken’s animosity is particularly inflamed by the Kemets, driving it to purge both them and the Kepesh from the waters it claims.
theocracy-of-kepesh-bright-coast.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

theocracy-of-kepesh-brightlight-desert.name: Brightlight Desert
theocracy-of-kepesh-brightlight-desert.description: The Kingdom of Shahar was a mighty realm during the Ancient and Malrokian Ages. However, the Malrokian Curse has destroyed it. The scattered ruins, broken stone towers, and bronze dome fragments serve as remnants of its former glory. Sometimes the shifting sands uncover some of its ancient ruins with riches that attract explorers. Now, it’s a barren land with dangerous nagas, cunning rakshasas, and tribes of salamanders who share the land with the few survivors of Shahar. The human survivors split into three tribes, the Sirocchi, Zaphyrus, and Verdane. Each tribe blames the others for their land not recovering. Adorned in long robes and armed with curved blades, they became barbarian tribes, and their cultures diverged over centuries of strife. However, they still share some customs, such as honoring the dead through martial displays, and young warriors undergoing ritual combats and tests of endurance. The Sirocchi.Dwellers on high cliffs near the Ubelian Fire Pits, build fortress homes carved on cliff walls and live by stringent laws. Their warriors, sword and shield experts, braid steel chains in their hair and use white robes bearing family emblems. In grand halls, they debate law and community under their King’s gaze. They worship Tamera, but not as part of the Celestianist Church, as they deem Bauron evil. They yearn for a united Shahar and believe Tamera’s blessing will return with restored order. The Zaphyrus.These nomads wander the sands, expressing their love for freedom through their foldable silk tents and martial dances. They follow the Glorious One, believing he is the true sun’s god, and view Tamera’s faith as oppressive. Generous and cunning, they avoid violence, seeing Shahar’s fall as a lesson against greed for power. They resist restoring the kingdom, linking such ambitions to Tanares’ calamities. They advocate peace and individual freedom to appease the gods. They believe that the Verdani and Sirocchi must lay down their weapons for them all to be blessed again. The Verdani.They live in tune with the harsh desert, mastering falconry, and building homes from sandstone and plant fibers with roofs designed to collect dew. Their culture prizes the natural order, where strength reigns. They attack those they see as weak or civilized, believing that eliminating these elements will rejuvenate the desert. Their brutal view of the Nature’s Spirit faith celebrates the survival of the fittest. They are the most dangerous and brutal of the tribes, attacking travelers, merchants, and other tribes at any opportunity to prove their strength and “curb the weak”. They believe that once they kill all the Sirocchi, who dare to keep laws and a king, and all the Zaphyrus, who are cowards unwilling to let go of their traditions to embrace nature, the desert will again flourish with natural power. To make their conflict worse, water disputes are fueling animosity, with Sirocchi canals redirecting essential resources, prompting clashes. Allied to that a mysterious sickness at the oases is causing the tribes to blame one another, each trying to find a cure hidden within desert secrets and the Shahar’s ruins. The Suns’ Scroll, prophesying Shahar’s resurgence, was found by the Sirocchi, it talks about a foreigner that will uncover ancient secrets. Their king is searching for this chosen one, giving special attention to warriors and adventurers from other lands.
theocracy-of-kepesh-brightlight-desert.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

theocracy-of-kepesh-hag-salar.name: Hag’Salar
theocracy-of-kepesh-hag-salar.description: Amidst the dunes and stone remnants lies the ruins of the Summer Elves Kingdom of Hag’Salar, once a splendid realm remembered for its cultural diversity and trading. Though the civilization has crumbled, its spirit endures, as the ruins are a meeting point for cultural exchange. The Alchemist Oasis, located within Hag’Salar, has become a sacred site for all barbarian communities of the south. Combat is strictly forbidden here, fostering peace and becoming a hub of commerce among the tribes. Every year during the summer solstice, a ten-day bazaar takes place in Hag’Salar. Tribes, merchants, and caravans from different lands assemble here, setting up their tents and stalls and transforming the desert into a vast marketplace. Most Summer elves visit this bazaar at least once every five years to reconnect with each other and exchange goods, knowledge, and stories from their voyages across the continent. During these events, tribes forge alliances and buy products from across Tanares. The absence of external laws grants a unique freedom, permitting the trade of goods otherwise restricted in different regions. Recently, the Kepesh have also turned their attention to this celebration. They propagate the faith of Ba-Ka and recruit from among the barbarians and the marginalized, integrating them into Kepesh society. Yet, the Kepesh approach cautiously, knowing well the potential threat of the barbarians to their expansionist aims. Another allure of this land is the treasures of the ancient Summer elves, which can be found in its lost ruins. The Kepesh often organize expeditions into the subterranean depths, bestowing lesser artifacts and gold to the barbarians to ensure cooperation. Some adventurers and explorers often travel here in search of treasures. Still, they must contend with the Kepesh, who want to keep the prizes for their Pharaoh, and the barbarians, who dislike intruders in their territories.
theocracy-of-kepesh-hag-salar.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

theocracy-of-kepesh-pakaitos-the-new-cap.name: Pakaitos, the new Capital
theocracy-of-kepesh-pakaitos-the-new-cap.description: The Kepesh capital is a splendid city erected upon golden sands, encircled by towering sandstone walls glistening under the desert sun. The city’s layout features broad, orderly streets leading to an expansive plaza, with the central pyramids and temples dedicated to Ba-Ka, containing extensive libraries, mystical laboratories, and sacred vaults. The city’s design, encompassing the walls, streets, and temples, forms a vast magical circle that channels Ba-Ka’s divine grace, bestowing potent mystical defenses. The outer walls resist most magic, the water remains perpetually pure, and spellcasters recover their magical energies much quicker. Despite the blistering heat and sporadic sandstorms, the mystical barrier wards off the sand and also maintains Pakaitos’ relative comfort, hot for those non-accustomed but colder than the desert around. Beneath the city lie chambers where extraplanar elementals of diverse kinds are bound by magic. Wizards and clerics harness these elementals to forge magic items and conduct grandiose rituals. The urban structure reflects its rigid societal hierarchy, with concentric circles divided by walls, each representing a different caste. The bustling outer rings teem with markets offering exotic spices, magic items, and the unique handicrafts of Kepesh’s artisans, including elaborate jewelry and distinctively fashioned ceramics. Nonetheless, Pakaitos faces a threat from the Cult of the Shadow Wing. The resurgence of Ba-Ka worship worries the Ungods, prompting them to dispatch servants to undermine the Kepesh capital. As the city welcomes numerous refugees annually, the Cult has infiltrated occult cells within. The Hidden Cult operates among the Servants Caste, the Purple Witches blend in with the Wizards Caste, the Shadow Lords tempt several Ba-Ka’s clerics with greater power, and the Spawners of Droggath use the barbarian tribes against Kepesh’s farmlands and traders. The Pharaoh personally confronts these foes or delegates his most loyal servants to combat them, but the Cult’s assaults are unyielding. Lacking sufficient capable adherents to counter all threats, the Lich offers substantial rewards in gold or magic items to adventurers and mercenaries from distant lands willing to help suppress the Cult.
theocracy-of-kepesh-pakaitos-the-new-cap.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

theocracy-of-kepesh-the-great-nothing.name: The Great Nothing
theocracy-of-kepesh-the-great-nothing.description: The southern deserts are extremely dangerous, with enormous sandworms hunting in the dunes, giant scorpions foraging for food, and lamias claiming ancient ruins as their lairs. The mountains to the south harbor fierce barbarian tribes who traverse the desert for annual raids; they brave the sands, which serve as a natural defense against any incursions on their villages, to pillage the towns to the north and other barbarian tribes of the near regions. Many legends permeate the desert, but the most renowned speaks of an oasis whose waters can transmute metal into gold, heal any curse or ailment, and even resurrect the deceased. Countless adventurers seek this miraculous site annually, yet the oasis eludes discovery, its precise location and true capabilities eluding explorers. In reality, the oasis does exist but proves elusive, as a mystical sandstorm envelops it every three dawns, transporting it to a new location in the desert. The vigilant guardianship of numerous sphinxes further complicates access. These guardians consider it their sacred duty to protect the waters, permitting only those they judge as worthy. They challenge aspirants with questions to gauge their righteousness, tasks to measure their courage and integrity, and riddles to test their wisdom. Those failing the tests are turned away, and any who dare to approach the waters without consent are met with lethal consequences. Some scholars believe the oasis was created by drops of blood from the gods; others think it is a tear of Tamera or that it holds an artifact left by the angels. The truth is only known to the sphinxes, but they never disclosed it while seemingly waiting for something or someone and allowing very few to use its water’s power.
theocracy-of-kepesh-the-great-nothing.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

tsvetan-bone-fields.name: Bone Fields
tsvetan-bone-fields.description: The Strong Fist clan traditionally cultivates food where they bury their fallen warriors, adorning the site with the bones of giant beasts. They believe the food will absorb the essence of the fallen warriors and strengthen people. At the end of each day, shamans perform a blessing ritual, asking for the spirits to help the plants grow. However, the scent of their dead warrior attracts undead creatures at night, occasionally resulting in attacks against the shamans. As tradition demands, orcs are forbidden from battling within these sacred grounds, so the shamans are in search of external help to solve the problem.
tsvetan-bone-fields.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

tsvetan-eferhild-citadel.name: Eferhild Citadel
tsvetan-eferhild-citadel.description: Once known as the Cauldron of Moritar, the place was a fortress of the Mystical Kingdom, full of arcane protections that remain until today. The place is near a lava river, favoring metal weapons and armor creation. Katar and Mother Grizza reside there, harnessing the site’s potent magic to enhance all shamanic abilities. Influenced by the shamanic tradition, each resident has a totem in their home and meditates to contact their guardian animal spirit. Katar tries to improve the lives of the people; despite not being wealthy, food and water are distributed, and people are asked to work properly to ensure the services and basic needs of everyone. One particular shaman named Martuk claims that he can use spirits of magical beasts for his protection, and they are much more potent but demand some special actions to bound, often involving either the killing of individuals or causing significant destruction. Secretly, he is gathering more followers every day. This city also has an immense dungeon full of lava and protection from the wizards of the past. Some orcs have attempted to explore it, but none have successfully navigated its depths. Mother Grizza believes something important is hidden there, but she and Katar cannot afford to be absent for days exploring the site.
tsvetan-eferhild-citadel.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

tsvetan-feargus-the-capital.name: Feargus, the Capital
tsvetan-feargus-the-capital.description: A city founded during the Fallen Age has seen better days. After the Imperial retreat, the city’s economy was greatly shaken. Many tents cover the open areas of the city, providing precarious shelter for its residents. Additionally, some structures made of wood and bone are suspended by ropes from elevated places, housing families. Security and various services are offered by groups of mercenaries and specialists from the clans, usually favoring those who can pay more. The city Arena is constantly being used to settle disputes between families and groups, usually ending up with some deaths. In contrast, Vharzog’s palace stands out as the sole magnific and opulent structure in the city, full of music and food. Xateri and her shamans reside in the palace, which is heavily fortified to prevent acts of rebellion. Vharzog enjoys this situation, as he can now stimulate the orcs’ brutal instinct through poverty. With no more nobles left to label as ‘the villains,’ he pins the blame on Katar, effectively creating an army through his manipulation.
tsvetan-feargus-the-capital.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

tsvetan-obsidian-fortress.name: Obsidian Fortress
tsvetan-obsidian-fortress.description: Obsidian Fortress is an imposing construction, built entirely from the cooled and shaped volcanic glass. Its reflective walls glow with fiery colors from the nearby molten flow. Nearby, numerous small ember islands float in the river, resisting its current as if the fortress magically attracts them. The fortress served as a place to imbue weapons and magic items with animal spirits, but this practice was forbidden by the last Red Mother and the place was abandoned. However, now that she is dead, some Mage Tower members have much interest in capturing the spirits in the Astral Plane, and then binding them in the Fortress, as powerful items could be produced from it. The place is dangerous, as the heat, steam vents, and lava explosions are common. Furthermore, legends speak of an undead shaman guardian patrolling the fortress
tsvetan-obsidian-fortress.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

tsvetan-poison-grounds.name: Poison Grounds
tsvetan-poison-grounds.description: The Stone Fangs clan are experts in poisons and herbalism. They extract the substance from giant scorpions, giant snakes, and basilisks. Some refined poisons are extracted from the tails of imprisoned young purple worms and from green dragons. Agents of the clan are consistently hiring adventurers to hunt these creatures and bring them alive, paying some considerable amount of gold, even though the funds often come from pillaging. On other occasions, a beast might escape, causing destruction in the area.
tsvetan-poison-grounds.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

tsvetan-the-greatwolf-race-course.name: The Greatwolf Race Course
tsvetan-the-greatwolf-race-course.description: This annual event is celebrated by the Spiked Bones clan, where their best riders compete to test their agility, speed, and endurance. Other clans, or even individuals of any species, are also welcome to take on the challenge. Mounted on a Dire Wolf, it starts on the Cave of Sacrifice and ends on the Stormgrounds, covering almost all Tsvetan. It is more than a race; many perils are on the way, such as natural hazards, attacks from wild beasts, sabotage from rival competitors and clans, among other challenges The prize is a special paint from the First Red Mother’s creations, heavily guarded by the clan. It can fully protect for a single day from any penumbral effects and give resistance to all damage taken by penumbral creatures.
tsvetan-the-greatwolf-race-course.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

yama-floating-markets.name: Floating Markets
yama-floating-markets.description: In many cities and villages, traditional shops on boats resemble small red houses anchored in the middle of rivers. Many of these boats sell exotic teas made by rare herbs that can uplift the spirit (its cost range from 50 gp to 200 gp). To activate their powers, on a ceremony, all participants say the word Kampai and drink simultaneously. Then, a ceremonial master casts a specific spell, reciting the name of Tenshikin, and the effects last for 4 hours. The herbs can be obtained in Yama Bunkatsu forest. The warrior caste commonly consumes: Tea of Cherry Blossom. The spirit becomes lighter. The creature’s speed increases by 10 feet, and it can walk in water and difficult terrain with no penalties. Tea of Lotus. The spirit becomes resolved. Your attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 17, 18, 19, or 20. Tea of Plum Blossom. The spirit becomes protected. The creature has advantage on saving throws against spells and gains the Deflect Arrow ability (see monk’s class and consider a character level instead of monk level).
yama-floating-markets.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

yama-kagemori-village.name: Kagemori Village
yama-kagemori-village.description: Located at Yama’s southernmost point, Kagemori village has become a haunted place after the unearthing of a cursed Katana. Some believe it is a weapon used during the Ungods’ invasion; others assume this weapon came from the demons. During the day, it is a peaceful but empty village with many arts in porcelain and tapestries. A beautiful lake and cherry blossom trees stand out. At night, all this art becomes distorted, and evil spirits roam the place, seeking to consume souls. Among them are yūrei (vengeful spirits), kappa (water spirits that lure travelers to drown), and kodama (ancient tree spirits bringing misfortune to travelers). A cave leads to a vast labyrinthine dungeon where the katana is believed to be kept, and even nature becomes treacherous (as an example, the cherry blossoms fall continuously, putting the adventurers into a deep slumber). One common type of creature in the place is the jiangshi, usually with white and green skin and a paper talisman on its head.
yama-kagemori-village.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

yama-tengoku-palace-and-kinshi-the-forbi.name: Tengoku Palace and Kinshi, the forbidden city
yama-tengoku-palace-and-kinshi-the-forbi.description: From the golden gates of Yamanoma, a path leads to the Tengoku Palace, where the relics of the gods are hidden, along with an array of other mystical items and tameranium. The road is paved with golden tiles, adorned with arches bearing red lanterns, each marked with the emblem of Fumetsu Eido. Many guardians are on the way, some human monks and priests, others unnatural as Shisa (Lion-dog statues that come to life when intruders approach), and tameranium dragons. There is another protection on the artifacts. When close to any of them, a hundred other copies appear, and the legends say the guidance for the correct one comes from the pure heart. If the wrong one is taken, a Spirit Guardian possesses one of the samurai statues and attacks the robbers. There are only three objects that can reveal the correct artifact: the Jade Dragon Statuettes.
yama-tengoku-palace-and-kinshi-the-forbi.frameBasis: Label visually checked on its own parent illustration, 7 October 2026.

yama-tiger-monastery.name: Tiger Monastery
yama-tiger-monastery.description: Located atop a cold, hard-to-access mountain, the Tiger Monastery lies hidden within a dense bamboo forest. Although the rigorous cold surrounds the structure, the Ki energy maintains a pleasant temperature within. This structure is built from deep orange and black stones, with some large training grounds and places for meditation. Their main focus is honor, peace, and Ki studies. Legends tell about the Ancient Tiger ofuda, a special technique, capable of improving the Ki channeling beyond common limitations. Also, at night, monks report hearing the Whispering Bamboo, which is said to speak knowledge from ancient times to those who perform tasks to the spirits guarding it. Many families of the Goukuden clan dream of their children being admitted to the Monastery. Annually, the Festival of Tiger Masks displays many combats and admits new students from the most capable ones.

yama-yama-bunkatsu-forest.description: It a place full of dangers, especially the four Oni Guardians, typically forcing any reason for attacking. Blue Oni. Guardian of the trees and other plants. Red Oni. Guardian of animals and wildlife. Wet Oni. Guardian of streams and waterfalls Mountain Oni. Guardian of treasures and gems Many adventurers are hired to get their herbs and explore treasures of the forest, as some sugenjas believe another angelic artifact is hidden within Yama Bunkatsu.

yama-yamanoma.name: Yamanoma
yama-yamanoma.description: The capital of Yama stands majestic, fit for epic tales; its architecture is built into the slopes of Hihashiyama, as if ascending a stairway to heaven. Its districts, constructed on rising plateaus, mirror the social hierarchy of its inhabitants, with Tenshikin’s palace at the pinnacle. The city has grown and expanded recently because of economic progress, though foreign visitors are still limited. Resounding gongs mark the rhythm of activities, signaling both regular routines and special events. The high priests receive their Edicts and undertake actions to fulfill Tenshikin’s will. Although the city is generally safe, many hidden dangers lurk in the shadows, such as kitsunes, spectral ninjas, corrupted monks, and more. One interesting place in the city is the Silver Dragon Pagoda. Tenshikin allows criminals seeking redemption to undergo the test of the Silver Dragon. It is a construction that takes individuals to another plane in an immense tower of eleven floors, as large as a city. The test consists of reaching the pagoda rooftop and finding the portal to return to the Material Plane. Each floor presents a unique test, from combating unusual creatures and guardians to learning and demonstrating specific skills, and resisting temptations to act dishonorably. The challenges become progressively difficult to test the prisoner’s convictions, eventually leading them to challenge the Silver Dragon itself. Many die trying to reach the goal, but according to the few survivors, the hardest challenge is the seventh floor, the Lantern Library, capable of driving people insane. The secret of this tower is that people can be released from it through a demonstration of honor or altruism, not by defeating the challenges. Medium fey (shapechanger), any chaotic Armor Class: 13 Hit Points: 44 (8d8 + 8) Speed: 30 ft. STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (+0) 17 (+3) 12 (+1) 14 (+2) 15 (+2) 16 (+3) Skills: Deception +5, Insight +4, Perception +4, Stealth +5 Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 14 Languages: Common, Sylvan Challenge: 3 (700 XP) Shapechanger. The kitsune can use its action to polymorph into a human form, or back into its true form. Its statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Keen Hearing and Smell. The kitsune has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell. Innate Spellcasting. The kitsune’s innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 13). The kitsune can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: - At will: minor illusion - 3/day each:charm person, disguise self, illusionary script, invisibility, major image Actions Multiattack. The kitsune makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws. Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. Claws. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage.

undertanares.name: The Undertanares
undertanares.description: Réseau souterrain aussi vaste que le continent : champignons bioluminescents, rivières de magma, forêts de cristal, lacs et anciennes salles naines. Les sources ne fixent pas un plan continu des tunnels ni un contrôle politique unique. Vue d'ensemble de l'environnement, sans tracé inventé d'un itinéraire continental.

darkall.name: Continent of Darkall
darkall.description: Continent séparé de Tanares par l'Eternal Storm, tombée il y a vingt ans. Au nord : cités-États kemets et ruines pyramidales. Au centre : places fortes, villes fortifiées et terres désolées squelettiques. Au sud : Demonic Lands, deux portails vers les Abysses et neuf forteresses de seigneurs démons. Son contour et sa position ne sont pas fixés sur la carte mondiale VTT : vue d'ensemble sans côte, coordonnées ou distances inventées.

darkall-north.name: The North — Darkall
darkall-north.description: Nord de Darkall : cités-États kemets, ancienne terre des Kepesh et ruines pyramidales. Aucun plan précis de cité ni contour régional n'est établi. Vue d'ensemble du paysage documenté, sans nouvelle cité nommée.
darkall-north.frameBasis: Author audit bands with adjacent, non-overlapping boundaries.

darkall-central.name: Central Darkall
darkall-central.description: Centre de Darkall : places fortes, villes fortifiées et Wasteland squelettique, affecté par l'Elemental Maelstrom. Aucun emplacement précis de forteresse ni salle n'est établi. Les limites restent non cartographiées.
darkall-central.frameBasis: Author audit bands with adjacent, non-overlapping boundaries.

darkall-demonic-lands.name: Demonic Lands
darkall-demonic-lands.description: Sud de Darkall : territoires démoniaques comprenant deux portails vers les Abysses et neuf forteresses de seigneurs démons. Leurs noms, empreintes et positions ne sont pas établis. Préserver le nombre documenté sans dessiner une disposition précise inventée. Vue d'ensemble du paysage, limites non cartographiées.
darkall-demonic-lands.frameBasis: Author audit bands with adjacent, non-overlapping boundaries.

darkall-cave-of-the-damned.name: The Cave of the Damned
darkall-cave-of-the-damned.description: Caverne nommée dans les Demonic Lands de Darkall. Aucun plan de salles ou réseau de tunnels n'est établi : vue de la caverne et de son environnement, sans embranchements ou accès ajoutés.

mystical.name: Mystical — The Wasteland
mystical.description: Ancien Mystical Kingdom situé entre Yama, Sindile, Tsvetan, Central Empire et Seashores. Terres violettes maudites, ruines et morts-vivants. Le centre contient les ruines de l'ancienne capitale Arcana ; les bordures sont moins corrompues. Garder les limites, reliefs, rivières et positions de la référence VTT. Le contrôle local des cultistes sur toute la région n'est pas établi.

mystical-central.description: Centre du Wasteland de Mystical : territoire maudit violet, anciennes ruines du royaume, présence de morts-vivants. Aucune nouvelle ville, côte, salle ou forteresse nommée ne doit être ajoutée.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: The Parliament
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 1- The Parliament.The Republic’s heart is its political core, symbolized by a grand white marble edifice representing peace and hope. It hosts public debates, but some chambers are exclusive for confidential parliamentarian discussions. Recently, bills regulating certain aspects of magic use and altering taxes on specific goods have heightened Parliament tensions, leading some to secretly hire mercenaries to intimidate rivals.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: The Arena of Future
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 2- The Arena of Future. While no longer part of the judicial system, it remains a popular spectacle. Adventurers display their prowess in safe, magical, non-lethal bouts, seeking renown. Monthly tournaments in the Arena promise rich rewards, and victories here can elevate one’s status in the Adventurer’s Guild, unlocking more lucrative quests. Yet beneath its surface lies an inactive Vandanamalika, coveted by the Kemets and other powers. To activate it, specific pylons must be erected in the Storm Islands, Stravian, and Tsvetan.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Republic Military Fortress
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 3- Republic Military Fortress. Built atop a natural plateau, this fortress houses both magical cannons in its towering spires and the headquarters for the Freelands’ military forces. Sedura, the present Minister of Defense, devises strategies here that influence the entire army. Due to its key importance in defending the city from naval attacks, security here is reinforced. Nevertheless, the Kemets plot to disable the cannons, aiming to unleash their vast naval fleet to bombard defensive structures.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Prime Minister’s Palace
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 4- Prime Minister’s Palace. The palace is the home for the head of government and hosts meetings with diplomats and private talks with parliament members. It also serves as the administrative heart of many ministries and offices for the Republic’s state bodies. The Prime Minister traditionally holds a monthly gala here, attended by parliamentarians, wealthy merchants, diplomats, select nobles, and the families of those guests. These events are central to the Republic’s political maneuvers but are also exploited by groups like the Third Eye for negotiation, information gathering, intimidation, or even poisoning targets.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Celestianist Cathedral of Sun and Moon
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 5- Celestianist Cathedral of Sun and Moon. High Cardinal Taram oversees the Republic’s primary Celestianist temple, having shifted the Church’s administrative heart from the sacred Skybell to Fisherman’s Wharf. Though Skybell’s cathedral remains grand and the city is considered sacred, Taram’s choice represents a shift from using Church’s wealth as a display of power to now aid the populace. This temple is now the epicenter for Church deliberations, where Cardinals gather for them. With the ever-present danger of Ungods’ servants infiltrating society and the Church, Taram and the cardinals remain watchful. He discreetly enlists hero groups proven loyal to Tamera and Bauron to investigate dubious figures in the city.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Fisherman’s Wharf Port
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 6- Fisherman’s Wharf Port.The Republic’s largest and most militarized port is vital for its citizens, providing an abundance of fish and seafood like squid, octopus, and oysters. Most trade ships engage with Kolbjörn, as the Republic’s main trade flows through the Central Seas’ Goldraft port. Fishing boat captains frequently post tasks in the Adventurer’s Guild, needing aid against threats like Kemet vessels, Sahuagin clans, the occasional kraken, or pirates responsible for vanishing ships.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Seabreeze District
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 7- Seabreeze District. This middle-class enclave houses merchants, artisans, fishing ship owners, military officers, and bureaucrats. It’s a serene district where children play in the streets and neighbors know each other by name. Businesses are restricted to those meeting basic daily needs, such as bakeries and small food vendors.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: The Six Quarters
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 8- The Six Quarters.Surrounding the Parliament, this district boasts the city’s priciest estates. These grand homes belong to parliamentarians, nobles, and affluent merchants. No commercial endeavors are allowed. The sole non-residential structure is the esteemed Relic Hunters Guild headquarters, housing Tanares’ most renowned open museum. Given the guild’s collection of ancient treasures and vast knowledge from Tanares’ ruins, it is heavily defended, with many magical traps and mystical sentinels protecting its vaults. While heists have been attempted, the guild has consistently secured its relics.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Wallside District
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 9- Wallside District. Inhabited by winter elves, this district is eyed with mistrust by the city’s denizens, doubting the residents’ true loyalties. Though most are innocent winter elves, some Kemet spies blend in, masquerading as regular townsfolk. A concealed temple to Bás lies in a house basement where these Kemets convene to venerate their god. They covertly plan to bring frost to the farms, leading to food scarcity and city weakening. With discretion, they place secret shrines of Bás across the farmlands, awaiting the impending winter to activate their sabotage plan.
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.frameBasis: Cadre graphique releve sur la reconstruction isometrique du 6 octobre 2026 ; aucune coordonnee de scene.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Uptown
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 10- Uptown. Nestled among hilly terrain with uneven and sometimes steep streets, the area boasts diverse shops, homes, and artistically designed estates. The city’s open market thrives in the southeast on cobblestone grounds. Overlooking the market, atop a hill, stands the Adventurer’s Guild headquarters, a central hub for adventurers. Its mission board is perpetually filled, offering quests ranging from monster hunts to herb collections, merchant escorts through perilous areas, and even journeys to distant lands. Each task offers rewards proportional to its risks and duration, with values set by the quest givers. However, underpriced quests may remain unclaimed

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: Hope Square
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 11- Hope Square.Home to laborers and farming families, the district boasts modest dwellings, many crafted from resilient timber salvaged from the buildings destroyed during the Kemet Invasion. Those who lost their homes in the war resettled in Fisherman’s Wharf, naming this district. On its edge stands the Fisherman’s Wharf Academy of Magic, a symbol against the Empire’s stranglehold on the study of magic. While this district embodies hope, it also harbors a darker aspect. As this is one of the city’s most impoverished areas, crime is rife. Nights are treacherous, with muggings rampant and the murder toll exceeding the city’s combined. The government’s bid to strengthen patrols falters against the needed manpower and costs. Skirmishes between guards and criminals intensify, as these rogues band together, their menace growing.

republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.name: The Cerulean Plaza
republic-of-freelands-fisherman-s-wharf-.description: 12- The Cerulean Plaza. The commercial heart of Fisherman’s Wharf, this bustling market is brimming with local and imported wares. Adorned with inns, taverns, and the grand “Cerulean Cross Hotel,” the plaza boasts a uniform white and blue facade, enforced on the owners by fines. Celebrated as one of Tanares’ most beautiful marketplaces, its elegant shops, filled with exotic goods, attract many wealthy patrons, as well as bandits. With crime on the rise, shopkeepers, weary of the overburdened authorities, now turn to adventurers, offering rewards for reclaiming stolen items.

central-empire-the-capital-city.name: La Capitale
central-empire-the-capital-city.description: Une ville continue : huit quartiers dans les murs, quatre faubourgs et les docks. Oldtown est sur l’autre rive de la Rubicund River ; les quartiers intérieurs se raccordent par leurs rues.

central-empire-the-capital-city-sloghood.name: Sloghood
central-empire-the-capital-city-sloghood.description: Faubourg hors les murs, soigné, ruelles étroites, couleurs des maisons nobles, ancienne foi Evolutionist. South Creek à gauche ; Uptown à droite derrière le mur ; Bloomburgs en bas.

central-empire-the-capital-city-uptown.name: Uptown
central-empire-the-capital-city-uptown.description: Quartier intra-muros des petits nobles et artistes, manoirs distincts, galeries, pavés sinueux et lanternes. Tsvetown mêle les traditions orques et impériales. Sloghood à gauche, Palacedomain en haut, Artisansquare à droite, Bloomburgs en bas hors les murs.

central-empire-the-capital-city-artisans.name: Artisansquare
central-empire-the-capital-city-artisans.description: Quartier intra-muros de guildes rivales et ateliers ornés, sculptures et jardins. The Vault est la banque, pas un palais. Uptown à gauche, Downtown en haut, Scholarnest à droite, Bloomburgs en bas hors le mur.

central-empire-the-capital-city-scholarn.name: Scholarnest
central-empire-the-capital-city-scholarn.description: Quartier intra-muros universitaire socialement mixte, bâtiments de marbre blanc, statues de Torygg et Baleroth, théâtres et logements étudiants. Downtown en haut à gauche, Artisansquare à gauche, Dweomer à droite, Neckoffoods en bas hors les murs.

central-empire-the-capital-city-dweomer.name: Dweomer
central-empire-the-capital-city-dweomer.description: Quartier intra-muros arcanique : grands manoirs, jardins, cristaux de protection et lanternes flottants, golems de pierre présentés comme statues. Martpart en haut, Scholarnest à gauche, Neckoffoods en bas et à droite hors les murs.

central-empire-the-capital-city-martpart.name: Martpart
central-empire-the-capital-city-martpart.description: Quartier intra-muros commerçant, architecture culturellement métissée et plus dense que les manoirs d’Arenarea, étals à lanternes et pavés. Arenarea en haut à gauche, Downtown à gauche, Scholarnest en bas à gauche, Dweomer en bas. Rubicund River longe uniquement le bord haut/droit ; Oldtown sur l’autre rive.

central-empire-the-capital-city-arenarea.name: Arenarea
central-empire-the-capital-city-arenarea.description: Quartier intra-muros noble et monumental, manoirs à colonnes de marbre, jardins de façade et fontaines. Arena of Fate près de la baie en haut, Dusk of Justice au pied de l’arène. Natural Pool en bas à gauche de l’arène, casino plus bas, Hippodrome à droite et plus bas. Docks à gauche hors les murs, Oldtown en haut à droite au-delà de la Rubicund River ; Palacedomain en bas à gauche, Downtown en bas, Martpart en bas à droite. Les quartiers se touchent par de vraies rues : Arenarea n’est pas une île.

central-empire-the-capital-city-oldtown.name: Oldtown
central-empire-the-capital-city-oldtown.description: Faubourg historique hors les murs sur la rive opposée à Arenarea et Martpart. Rue étroites, maisons vieillies d’héritage Orsal, industries anciennes. Cimetière et Moon Tower en haut, scierie à gauche, forges et abattoir à droite. Rubicund River en bas sépare le quartier de la ville impériale.

central-empire-the-capital-city-neckoffo.name: Neckoffoods
central-empire-the-capital-city-neckoffo.description: Faubourg agricole hors les murs, champs et fermes, anciens héros retraités. Braves Arena est une petite arène de débutants, pas un Colisée. Scholarnest et Dweomer au-dessus derrière le mur, Bloomburgs à gauche.

central-empire-the-capital-city-bloombur.name: Bloomburgs
central-empire-the-capital-city-bloombur.description: Faubourg pauvre de réfugiés hors les murs au-dessous d’Uptown et d’Artisansquare. Dédale de ruelles, logements serrés, marché noir. Les sous-quartiers sont Kjörners à gauche, The Worst au milieu/gauche et Ubelians à droite. Sloghood à gauche, Neckoffoods à droite.

central-empire-the-capital-city-downtown.name: Downtown
central-empire-the-capital-city-downtown.description: Cœur administratif et spirituel intra-muros. Cathédrale des Huit, Municipal Palace, hôpital, manoirs nobles, statues des divinités et héros sanctifiés. Arenarea au-dessus, Palacedomain à gauche, Martpart à droite, Artisansquare et Scholarnest en bas.

central-empire-the-capital-city-palacedo.name: Palacedomain
central-empire-the-capital-city-palacedo.description: Domaine impérial intra-muros et entouré de sa propre enceinte. Palais en haut du domaine, vastes jardins botaniques, lanternes magiques, voies réservées. Ironhand Headquarters et école de guerre plus bas, complexe de portails et temple de Tamera vers le bord gauche. Docks/Arenarea au-dessus, Downtown à droite, Uptown en bas, Sloghood hors les murs en bas à gauche.
